| [THEORY-082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-082.md) | Natural-gradient efficiency needs full-rank Fisher | Amari (1998), [LIT-607](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-607.md). Theorem 1 is a Lagrangian derivation: under \|dw\|² = Σg_ij dw_i dw_j the steepest-descent direction is −G⁻¹∇L, so it changes with G. Theorem 2 shows that online learning with step 1/t along the Fisher natural gradient attains the Cramér–Rao bound G⁻¹/t, and its proof uses G(w*)⁻¹. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), Eq. 14, calls a truth regular when the optimum is one point and its Fisher is positive definite, and singular otherwise. From Amari's own Eq. 6.12, the score for hidden unit i's input weights carries the factor v_i. So the Fisher of a multilayer perceptron loses rank wherever an output weight is zero. The claim that the Fisher is the only invariant metric is Chentsov's, cited and not held. | Active |
| [THEORY-084](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-084.md) v4 | Lazy Fisher inherits NTK harmonic blocks | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. The identity is linear algebra: JᵀJ (parameters × parameters) and JJᵀ (samples × samples) have the same non-zero eigenvalues. Under squared loss JᵀJ is the Gauss–Newton matrix and the Fisher. JJᵀ is the empirical NTK Gram matrix, which in the kernel regime on uniform spherical data has the degree-block spectrum of Bietti & Bach (2021), [LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md): µ_k with multiplicity N(d, k). The threshold claim draws on Cao et al. (2019), [LIT-624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-624.md). Their guarantees are stated only for whole eigenspaces, with sample costs that grow as the gap below them shrinks. It also draws on Basri et al. (2019), [LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md), where a structural zero block shows up in a finite sample as small non-zero eigenvalues. No paper filed computes a Fisher spectrum in this regime. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-134](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md) v3 | Viability kernel is the part that can persist | Aubin's viability theory, read in his 1999 mini-course notes [LIT-714](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-714.md). | [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) v4 | More informative iff simulable by randomisation | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorem 8 with Theorems 1–3: for experiments with finitely many states and decision problems with bounded losses, α attains every loss vector β attains, in every problem, exactly when a Markov kernel turns α's observation into β's under every state. | [THEORY-168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md) v4 | Contextuality depends on the representation | Dzhafarov, Cervantes & Kujala (2017), [LIT-790](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-790.md), with Dzhafarov & Kujala's CbD 2.0 ([LIT-831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-831.md)) and CbD 1.0 ([LIT-777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md)). The same measurements can receive different verdicts. Maximal and multimaximal couplings can disagree when a content appears in three or more contexts (four, for binary variables), and the record's worked case shows it. Multimaximal couplings of non-binary variables can be destroyed by coarse-graining. With every dichotomization kept, two content-sharing variables are contextual on their own unless one nominally dominates the other. The authors present the representation as the analyst's choice, not as a defect. What the record does not get from these papers is any rule for choosing it. | Active |
| [THEORY-171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md) v5 | Causal structure is a source of contextuality | From Gogioso & Pinzani's trilogy: The Topology of Causality, [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md), read in [NOTE-612](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-612.md), with the definitions of The Combinatorics of Causality, [LIT-800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-800.md) ([NOTE-635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-635.md)). Over a space of input histories with the lowerset topology, causal functions form a separated presheaf, and on the space Θ₃ it is not a sheaf: two causal assignments on disjoint opens give one event two outputs on their common extension. That example was checked here, and it settles the claim. The source's Theorem 2.34, that the presheaf is a sheaf exactly when no two contexts impose incompatible causal pasts on a common event, is reported as the source's. Adversaries are algorithms; the paper has no circuit version, and that the proof carries over to non-uniform adversaries is the reading's inference, not the paper's statement. Everything is asymptotic. Goldreich states the theorem and does not prove it. | Active |
| [THEORY-357](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-357.md) | Indistinguishable needn't mean statistically close | Goldreich, Foundations of Cryptography vol. 1, [LIT-1061](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1061.md), read in [NOTE-863](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-863.md) (Skimmed, 1995 draft, Chapters 1–3 in full), with Håstad, Impagliazzo, Levin and Luby (1999), [LIT-1051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1051.md), read in [NOTE-880](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-880.md). Proposition 3.3 proves by counting that some ensemble far from uniform fools every small circuit; its proof is non-constructive and the ensemble cannot be sampled efficiently. A generator's output is efficiently samplable, indistinguishable from uniform by definition, and statistically far by an image count (§3.3.1). That a samplable such pair exists only if one-way functions do is cited to Goldreich 1990, not read. The book's statistical difference has no factor ½, so it is twice total variation. | Active |
| [THEORY-366](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-366.md) | Concentrated distances make nearest ≈ farthest | Beyer, Goldstein, Ramakrishnan and Shaft (1999), [LIT-1099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1099.md), read in [NOTE-917](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-917.md) from the authors' 1998 technical report. Theorem 1: for n fixed data points and an independent query, var(d^p / E[d^p]) → 0 implies P[DMAX ≤ (1+ε)DMIN] → 1 for every ε > 0. The index m is arbitrary, so dimension enters only through the workload's distance distributions. IID coordinates and several correlated or non-identical workloads satisfy the condition; a diagonal line, two latent degrees of freedom and queries inside clusters do not. The condition is sufficient, not necessary. The result concerns the ratio of distances at fixed n, and does not show that real high-dimensional data loses contrast, or that indexes fail. | Active |
| [THEORY-369](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-369.md) v2 | Partitioning NN indexes lose to scans in high dim | Weber, Schek and Blott (1998), [LIT-1107](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1107.md), read in [NOTE-919](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-919.md). Under uniformity and independence, with the expected nearest-neighbour distance used as every query's radius and integrals evaluated by Monte Carlo, the fraction of blocks read passes the 20% line at about d = 15–20 for rectangular regions and 26 for spherical ones. A crude bound for any convex clustering puts it below 610. The often-quoted "around 10" is the measured crossover for an R*-tree and an X-tree. The VA-file, a scan of compact per-vector approximations, is the paper's alternative. Nothing is shown for data of low intrinsic dimension, and the finite-dimensional bounds are not rigorous as stated. The asymptotic statement, at fixed N and for clusters of two or more points, is proved by the record by a concentration argument. | Active |
| [THEORY-370](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-370.md) | Small-world search is fast only at r = 2 | Kleinberg (2000), [LIT-1103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1103.md), read in [NOTE-923](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-923.md). Proved for the two-dimensional lattice: with nodes, local links and the number of long-range links fixed, changing only the exponent r of the long-range link distribution moves the expected delivery time of the best decentralized searcher from O((log n)²) at r = 2 to a power of n at every other r, including r = 0, where paths of polylogarithmic length exist. The upper bound is proved only for one local and one long-range link per node; the k-dimensional statement (r = k) is asserted, not proved; the family is inverse power laws of a distance every node can compute, so it does not show that no other link structure is navigable. | Active |
| [THEORY-371](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-371.md) | CQ equivalence is homomorphism both ways | Chandra and Merlin (1977), [LIT-1111](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1111.md), read in [NOTE-907](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-907.md). Reading a conjunctive query as its natural model, equivalence becomes a pair of homomorphisms (Lemma 13), the minimal equivalent query is unique up to isomorphism (Theorem 12), and evaluation with the query as input is NP-complete (Theorem 7), as is deciding whether one query is a folding of another (Theorem 11). The paper states equivalence, not containment, and does not state that containment or equivalence is NP-complete; those are corollaries later work attributes to it. Nothing here reaches queries with equality, comparisons, negation or union. | Active |
| [THEORY-372](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-372.md) | ANN space–time trade-off is optimal for hashing | Andoni, Laarhoven, Razenshteyn and Waingarten (2017), [LIT-1120](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1120.md), read in [NOTE-918](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-918.md) from the arXiv full version. A data-dependent tree of spherical caps, with different thresholds for filing points and for routing queries, realizes every pair of exponents on the curve, for worst-case data, with constant success probability; the equal-threshold point is LSH. On random instances with d = ω(log n), list-of-points structures cannot beat the curve (a lower bound the paper calls conditional), and one- or two-probe cell-probe structures need n^{(c/(c−1))²−o(1)} words, the curve's space at ρq = 0. Optimality for data-dependent schemes, for more probes, and for d = Θ(log n) is not shown. The curve prices space against per-query time for one query at a time; it has no workload and no build cost beyond space. | Active |
| [THEORY-373](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-373.md) | Semiring provenance factors through polynomials | Green, Karvounarakis and Tannen (2007), [LIT-1110](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1110.md), read in [NOTE-913](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-913.md). Union and projection add tags, join multiplies them; the usual RA identities hold exactly when the tags form a commutative semiring, and a map of tags commutes with every query exactly when it is a semiring homomorphism. The polynomials N[X] are the free commutative semiring, so the annotated answer in any semiring is the polynomial answer evaluated at the input annotations (Theorem 4.3). It is a sufficiency result for revisions that re-annotate existing inputs, not a minimality result, and it excludes added facts and every nonmonotone operation. | Active |
| [THEORY-380](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-380.md) v3 | Datalog provenance is formal power series | Green, Karvounarakis and Tannen (2007), [LIT-1110](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1110.md), read in [NOTE-913](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-913.md). A recursive query can derive a tuple in infinitely many ways, so polynomials do not suffice and the semiring needs infinite sums. With ω-continuous semirings and the provenance semiring N∞⟦X⟧ the paper states the analogues of the relational results: a fixed-point characterization (Theorem 5.6), factorization (Theorem 6.4), and a test for infinite coefficients (Theorem 6.5), with algorithms that decide finiteness and compute coefficients. Proofs are not given. Plain N and N[X] are excluded, the provenance can be an infinite object held only as equations, and negation remains outside. | Active |
| [THEORY-381](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-381.md) | Fast near-neighbour queries need much more space | Panigrahy, Talwar and Wieder (2010), [LIT-1102](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1102.md), read in [NOTE-914](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-914.md) from the arXiv preprint. For graphical neighbour search, to which decision approximate near neighbour reduces, on data drawn so that neighbourhoods rarely overlap: deterministic t-probe structures satisfy (mwt/n)^t ≥ Φv and m^t·t·w/n ≥ Φv(1/m^t); randomized ones satisfy m^t·w/n ≥ Φr(1/m^t, γ/t) and (mwt⁴/n)^{2t} ≥ Φr(1/m, γ/t). On the hypercube this gives space n^{1+Ω(1/(ct))} at approximation c and n^{Ω(1/(tε²))} at 1 + ε; a one-probe structure matches on Cayley graphs; low-contention dynamic structures need update time at least Φr(τ, 1/(4t²)) over poly(t). Tight only for constant t; nothing about worst-case or structured data, workloads or build time. | Active |
| [THEORY-388](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-388.md) | LSH gives sublinear approximate NN queries | Indyk and Motwani (1998), [LIT-1106](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1106.md), read in [NOTE-905](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-905.md) from the authors' 1999 expanded version, compared with the STOC text. A hash family under which points within r1 collide with probability at least p1 and points beyond r2 with at most p2 gives n^ρ random tables, each storing every point: O(dn + n^{1+ρ}) space and O(n^ρ) hash evaluations per query, ρ = ln(1/p1)/ln(1/p2), for the decision version, which ring-cover trees connect to approximate nearest neighbour with polylog overhead. Bit sampling gives ρ ≤ 1/(1+ε) in Hamming space and, by embedding, ℓ_p for p in [1, 2]; the STOC text states 1/ε and only for ε > 1. Grid bucketing gives Õ(d) queries for n·O(1/ε)^d preprocessing. Preprocessing is counted as space. Nothing is proved about whether these exponents can be beaten. | Active |
| [THEORY-390](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-390.md) | JL concentration implies the RIP | Baraniuk, Davenport, DeVore and Wakin (2008), [LIT-1156](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1156.md), read in [NOTE-931](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-931.md) from the author-posted copy. The only assumption is the concentration inequality Pr(\|‖Φx‖² − ‖x‖²\| ≥ ε‖x‖²) ≤ 2e^{−nc₀(ε)}, met with Achlioptas's c₀(ε) = ε²/4 − ε³/6. The proof is the JL argument run over a net on every sparse support, plus a step from the net to the whole subspace. Necessity of k log(N/k) is recalled from Gelfand widths, not derived from concentration, and constants are implicit. | Active |
| [THEORY-391](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-391.md) v4 | Non-Gaussian ℓ₁ transitions approach Gaussian's | Donoho and Tanner (2009), [LIT-1160](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1160.md), read in [NOTE-933](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-933.md) from arXiv 0906.2530v1. The Gaussian transition is a theorem of the authors' earlier papers, restated here. The universality is an observation from 2,948,000 optimizations at N = 200, 400 and 1600: strict finite-N universality is rejected, and agreement as N → ∞ is not rejected. Sparse and Hadamard matrices sit about one transition width low at small N. The title states only what was measured. Whether the agreement is a limit theorem is QUESTION-168. | Active |
| [THEORY-392](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-392.md) v2 | Hilbert extensions cost at most √(log n) | Johnson and Lindenstrauss (1984), [LIT-1153](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1153.md), read in [NOTE-930](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-930.md). Theorem 1 proves Marcus and Pisier's conjecture L(X, n) ≤ K(Log n)^(1/2) for every metric space X; Theorem 3 gives L(p, n) ≥ δ(Log n/Log Log n)^(1/p−1/2) for 1 ≤ p < 2, hence L(∞, n) ≥ δ(Log n/Log Log n)^(1/2). The √(log n) comes from the √k cost of passing between ℓ₂ᵏ and ℓ∞ᵏ, with k of order log n. Whether the upper bound is sharp the paper leaves open, and the constants are loose. | Active |
| [THEORY-393](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-393.md) | Cross inner products embed below JL dimension | Alon and Klartag (2017), [LIT-1151](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1151.md), read in [NOTE-929](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-929.md) from arXiv v4. Theorem 1.2 answers, in a bipartite form, Larsen and Nelson's question whether log n can become log(2 + ε²n) in the JL lemma. The proof is convex geometry: Khatri–Šidák bounds the Gaussian measure of a body of slabs, and a weakened low M*-estimate puts a random t-dimensional subspace close to every scaled a_i. Conjecture 2.4, the same with norms O(1), is proved only for t of order n (Theorem 2.5). It is not an embedding of one point set and says nothing about distances. | Active |
| [THEORY-394](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-394.md) | Metrics embed in ℓ₂ with O(log n) distortion | Linial, London and Rabinovich (1995), [LIT-1155](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1155.md), read in [NOTE-928](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-928.md) from the authors' February 1995 manuscript. Theorem 3.2(1) states Bourgain's theorem ([LIT-1161](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1161.md), unread): every n-point metric embeds in O(log n)-dimensional Euclidean space with distortion O(log n). The paper reproves the distortion with a randomized map into ℓ_p^{O(log² n)} built from distances to O(log n) random sets of each size 2ˡ, and gets the dimension from Johnson–Lindenstrauss. Proposition 4.2 shows that every embedding of a constant-degree expander into ℓ_p, 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, has distortion Ω(log n), from the expander's Ω(log n) gap between flow and cut. Together these answer Johnson and Lindenstrauss's Problem 4 in the negative, which the paper does not say. | Active |
| [THEORY-395](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-395.md) v2 | JL dimension is optimal for worst-case sets | Larsen and Nelson (2017), [LIT-1154](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1154.md), read in [NOTE-925](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-925.md) from arXiv v2. Theorem 2 removes the lg(1/ε) gap that Welch, Levenshtein and Alon left, for arbitrary maps. The proof is an encoding argument over a family of k-sparse vectors with k ≈ ε⁻², ending at nm = Ω(kn lg(d/k)). It is a worst-case bound by existence with an untracked constant. It is not a phase transition, and the paper notes that ε-incoherent sets fit in o(ε⁻² lg n) dimensions for small enough ε. | Active |
| [THEORY-396](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-396.md) | Banach extensions cost O(log n/log log n) | Lee and Naor (2005), [LIT-1152](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1152.md), read in [NOTE-927](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-927.md) from the authors' January 2004 preprint. Theorem 1.10 (Theorem 5.1(4)): ae(X) ≤ C log n/log log n for every n-point metric space X, bounding the extension constant over every superspace and every Banach target at once, improving Johnson, Lindenstrauss and Schechtman's C log n. Theorem 1.12: eₙ(L_p, Z) ≤ C(p)(log n)^{1/p} for 1 < p ≤ 2, C√(log n) at p = 2, through the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma and e(ℓ₂ᵈ, Z) ≤ C√d. For Hilbert targets Johnson and Lindenstrauss's K√(log n) ([THEORY-392](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-392.md)) stays the better bound, and the paper states as open whether O(√(log n)) holds for every metric domain and normed target. | Active |
| [THEORY-397](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-397.md) | Random projections keep distances within 1 ± ε | Dasgupta and Gupta (2003), [LIT-1157](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1157.md), read in [NOTE-932](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-932.md), give the explicit bound for a projection onto a random subspace; Johnson and Lindenstrauss (1984), [LIT-1153](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1153.md), read in [NOTE-930](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-930.md), prove the lemma with k = [K(τ) log n] and K ≥ (10/τ)² by Lévy's isoperimetric inequality; Achlioptas, [LIT-1159](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1159.md), read in [NOTE-926](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-926.md) from a 2002 draft, carries the same k₀ to independent ±1 and sparse three-valued entries. The guarantee is for a fixed finite set, on squared distances, and it rests on entries being zero-mean. It says nothing about maps that go up in dimension or are followed by a threshold. | Active |
| [THEORY-398](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-398.md) v2 | Separated sets extend Lipschitz maps at O(D/ε) | Johnson and Lindenstrauss (1984), [LIT-1153](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1153.md), read in [NOTE-930](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-930.md). Theorem 2 gives 6D/ε for maps into ℓ₂, through ℓ₁ and a weak form of Grothendieck's inequality; Benyamini's appendix gives 4D/ε for any Banach target, through a retraction of ℓ∞(Γ) with Lipschitz constant at most 2. The bound trades the count of points for the spread of the set. Whether either constant is best possible is not discussed. | Active |
| [THEORY-399](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-399.md) | Inner-product sketches need Θ(n log n/ε²) bits | Alon and Klartag (2017), [LIT-1151](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1151.md), read in [NOTE-929](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-929.md) from arXiv v4. Theorem 1.1 gives the bits of an additive ε-distance sketch for every k when 1/n^0.49 ≤ ε ≤ 0.1, by a volume argument above and a packing of net points against random probes below. Since an embedding is a sketch, Corollary 2.1 re-proves Larsen and Nelson's bound in that range, and Corollary 2.3, using the Gaussian correlation inequality in place of a union bound, extends it to every ε ≥ 2/√n with log(2 + ε²n) in place of log n. The dimension statements are for additive error on squared distances of points of norm at most 1; the relative form for small ε follows but is not stated. The matching upper bound for one set is open. | Active |
| [THEORY-400](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-400.md) | Padded decompositions give Lipschitz extension | Lee and Naor (2005), [LIT-1152](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1152.md), read in [NOTE-927](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-927.md) from the authors' January 2004 preprint. Theorem 4.1 turns (ε, δ)-padded random partitions of the domain at every scale into a C/(εδ)-gentle partition of unity, and Lemma 2.1 turns that into extensions of constant 3C/(εδ) into any Banach space; Lemma 3.8 carries the partitions from X to any superspace. Theorem 5.1 gives ae(X) ≤ C log λ(X), ≤ C r² for K_r-minor-free graph metrics, ≤ C(g+1) on surfaces of genus g, and e(ℓ₂ᵈ, Z) ≤ C√d, generalizing Johnson, Lindenstrauss and Schechtman's Cd and Matoušek's trees. No lower bound shows any of them tight. | Active |
| [THEORY-401](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-401.md) | Numerosity gives a fair lottery on ℕ | Wenmackers (2011), [LIT-163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-163.md), chapter 2, read in [NOTE-139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md). P_num(A) = num(A)/α is defined on all of 𝒫(ℕ), gives each ticket 1/α > 0, and satisfies FAIR, ALL and a hypercountable form of SUM (eqs. 2.20–2.27). Proved, given the axiom of choice. It is not a free lunch: one solution per free ultrafilter, no invariance under relabelling, no countable additivity, and by the author's own admission it is empirically indistinguishable from the finitely additive real-valued solution. | Active |
| [THEORY-407](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-407.md) | Oseledets and drift hold with no curvature | Filip (2017), [LIT-093](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-093.md), expository notes read in full in [NOTE-078](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-078.md). Thm 2.2.6 is the Oseledets theorem, proved without Kingman; Thm 4.3.1 is the Karlsson–Ledrappier theorem, proved completely apart from cited measurable-selection results. Both are classical and not in doubt. The notes' own renditions of two other steps are flawed: Prop. 3.4.8(iii) is mis-stated, and the §5.3 tracking proof misapplies its lemma, so the Karlsson–Margulis and Kaimanovich forms should be cited to their originals. The hypotheses are ergodic stationary sampling and N → ∞. | Active |
| [THEORY-408](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-408.md) v3 | Gene frequencies track inclusive fitness | Hamilton (1964), Part I, [LIT-497](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-497.md), read in full in [NOTE-401](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-401.md). Each effect an individual causes falls partly on genes identical by descent with its own (weight r) and partly on others, which only dilute. So selection tracks inclusive fitness. The threshold is written −k > 1/r (§5), not rb > c: "more than two brothers, or four half-brothers, or eight first cousins". The maximization theorem needs non-negative total effects on others; for harming traits the change only points uphill. r is exact only for loci not under selection, and Hamilton could not bound the error (§4). | Active |
| [THEORY-420](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-420.md) | Rectangular weights' small singular values matter | Staats, Thamm & Rosenow (2024), [LIT-856](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-856.md), read in [NOTE-659](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-659.md). Freshly initialised matrices of BERT, Pythia and Llama follow the Marchenko–Pastur law; trained ones depart from it above the bulk, and, in rectangular matrices only, below it. Zeroing Llama-3 8B's smallest Down-Projection decile leaves 2.0% on GSM8K from 43.2%, worse than every decile but the largest, while the same decile of the square Attention-Output leaves 40.0%. Whether the below-bulk outliers are what carries the damage is not tested: the decile mixes them with the lower bulk, and overlap with the input's principal directions and ablation importance disagree for several matrix types. | Active |
| [THEORY-427](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-427.md) | Shampoo preconditions at least as full AdaGrad | Gupta, Koren and Singer (2018), [LIT-621](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-621.md), read in [NOTE-480](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-480.md). Lemma 8 is pure matrix analysis (operator monotonicity of the geometric mean); Theorems 7 and 10 give regret √(2r) D Tr(L^{1/4}) Tr(R^{1/4}), O(√T) when the spectral norm of the gradients is at most 1. Proved, in online convex optimisation, with D uncontrolled because the implementation omits the projection. Nothing here is a result about non-convex training; the deep network curves are four runs without seeds. | Active |
| [THEORY-430](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-430.md) | Arrangement region counts depend only on poset | Stanley (2006), [LIT-355](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-355.md), lecture notes read in full in [NOTE-313](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-313.md), with Lectures 1–2 and 6 read closely. Zaslavsky's theorem (Thm 2.5) is proved twice, by a deletion–restriction recurrence and by Euler characteristic; the bounded-region half has two unanswered "[why?]" steps in the first proof and an omitted fact in the second. Faces of every dimension are counted by Möbius values (Thm 2.6). The notes never use "topes" or "covectors", and do not cite Zaslavsky's own texts. A region is fixed by its side of each hyperplane only implicitly (p. 89). | Active |
| [THEORY-437](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-437.md) | Constrained-game equilibria need no convexity | Debreu (1952), [LIT-067](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-067.md), read in full in [NOTE-037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-037.md). The theorem (p. 888) is proved by applying the Eilenberg–Montgomery/Begle fixed-point theorem to the product of best-response correspondences. A Remark reduces the continuity of the value function to a compact graph plus continuity (lower hemicontinuity) of the constraint. It is existence only, in finite dimensions with finitely many agents and real-valued payoffs. That it contains Nash's theorem is asserted; the reduction is routine but not in the paper. | Active |
| [THEORY-441](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-441.md) | Problem of time doesn't make change illusory | Belot (2007), [LIT-122](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-122.md), read in [NOTE-118](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-118.md). A formal, not rigorous, derivation in the covariant phase-space formalism, with standard results cited. The vanishing Hamiltonian and the covariant derivation are strong; the canonical isomorphism of the reduced spaces is "presumed"; the claim that an artificially covariant theory escapes is hedged ("I think"). It is classical only. It diagnoses the problem and does not solve it. | Active |
| [THEORY-445](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-445.md) | Group convolutions are equivariant by design | Cohen & Welling (2016), [LIT-314](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-314.md), read in [NOTE-288](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-288.md). G-correlation commutes with the left action of G by the change of variables h → uh (eq. 12), and so do pointwise nonlinearities and pooling over cosets, up to edge effects and for rotations that are symmetries of the grid. Matched-parameter p4 and p4m layers lowered rotated-MNIST error from 5.03% to 2.28% and plain-CIFAR10 error from 9.45% to 6.46%. The paper uses no irreducible representations, characters or Fourier analysis, learns nothing about which symmetry the data have, and does not separate the effect of equivariance from the changed channel structure. | Active |
| [THEORY-456](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-456.md) | Ricci flow separates communities, but weakly | Ni, Lin, Luo & Gao (2019), [LIT-004](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-004.md), read in full with its SI in [NOTE-006](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-006.md), which checked Lemma E.1 by linear programming and iterated the proof's matrix. The flow w ← (1 − κ)d replaces each weight by the transport cost between the endpoints' neighbourhoods; bridge edges, with few shared neighbours, are negatively curved and grow. Theorem 4.1 (α = p = 0, cliques G(a,b), a > b ≥ 2) shows only non-gateway intra-clique edges shrinking; gateway edges grow at the inter-community rate with a ratio k ∈ (0,1) from Maple. Experiments use α = ½, p = 2, which no theorem covers. The Kesten–Stigum figure is [NOTE-006](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-006.md)'s calculation. | Active |
| [THEORY-474](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-474.md) | Toy-bit ZX calculus mirrors stabilizer theory | Backens & Duman (2014), [LIT-054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-054.md), read in full in [NOTE-066](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-066.md). A red–green spider calculus interpreted in the category of relations is universal and sound, and complete by Backens' stabilizer route. A binary matrix is a valid toy state iff SᵀJS = 0, the stabilizer condition (Lemma 3). The phase-free rules coincide with stabilizer ZX. That the phase group is the only categorical difference is cited, not shown, and completeness leans on analogy for several steps. The paper does no ψ-epistemic analysis and says nothing about which operational difference the phase group carries. | Active |
| [THEORY-478](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-478.md) v3 | Diffusion hyperbolic distance keeps local tree | Lin, Coifman, Mishne & Talmon (2023), [LIT-870](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-870.md), read in [NOTE-675](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-675.md). The hyperbolic diffusion distance is equivalent to min{1, d_T^(2α)} for 0 < α < 1/2 (Proposition C.4), under heat-kernel bounds on the tree that are cited rather than proved; one Hölder step holds only for d_T ≥ 1, and repaired, the reader finds the admissible range halves. Pairs beyond a radius are only known to be far, which matches the method's best mean average precision and its higher distortion than hyperbolic MDS on five graph benchmarks. A Euclidean distance on the same multiscale features does far worse. | Active |
| [THEORY-479](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-479.md) | Entropy is the unique information 1-cocycle | Baudot & Bennequin (2015), [LIT-053](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-053.md), read in [NOTE-088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-088.md). Theorems 1 and 3 are proved for finite spaces, through the Tverberg–Kendall–Lee result on measurable solutions of the fundamental equation of information. The hypotheses are stated three different ways in the paper; Theorem 1's is operative. The higher mutual informations appear as coboundaries, and Theorems B, D and F and the synergy reading are sketched or deferred to companion papers, so they are not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-486](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-486.md) | Family Floer equals GMN non-abelianization | Casals & Nho (2025), [LIT-017](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-017.md), an unrefereed v1 preprint read in full in [NOTE-022](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-022.md) by a reader who is not a Floer theorist. Theorems 1–3 are stated for any rank and for positive-braid asymptotics. The proofs cover exact Betti Lagrangians with finite creative networks; the meromorphic case adds hypotheses in prose, and the Family Floer functor is not built there. The analytic core is taken by citation from Ekholm 2007, which the authors patch, and from the second author's own preprint. Theorem 5, on networks from Demazure weaves, has no written proof and is not part of this account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-493](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-493.md) | Three axiom pairings yield GEM; Simons' doesn't | Varzi, SEP "Mereology" (2003, revised June 2026), [LIT-124](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-124.md), read in full in [NOTE-163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-163.md). A result the entry reports with citations (Hovda 2009; Cotnoir and Varzi 2019) and a countermodel (its Fig. 4; Pietruszczak 2000a, Pontow 2004), and which corrects Simons (1987), Casati and Varzi (1999) and the entry's own 2003 edition. The record has not checked the proofs. It is stated for first-order theories with a single primitive P and infinitary principles as axiom schemas, and it is a fact about axiom systems: it does not say classical mereology is true of anything. | Active |
| [THEORY-498](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-498.md) | Axioms holding isn't a structure of experience | Kleiner & Ludwig (2023; Synthese 2024), [LIT-143](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-143.md), read in full in [NOTE-135](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-135.md). The negative result is shown by construction: any set of aspects carries both the discrete topology and a coarser one, and a metric d passes whenever every C·d does. The replacement criterion (MSC) ties each relation to an aspect that co-varies with it under every variation. Its two positive cases rest on assumed transitivity and on the subsumptive unity thesis. The published version gives no structure that fails (MSC); the argument that metric spaces fail is in arXiv v1 only, and was withdrawn. | Active |
| [THEORY-502](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-502.md) | Forman curvature is a local degree statistic | Weber, Saucan & Jost (2016; J. Complex Networks 2017), [LIT-020](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-020.md), read in full in [NOTE-026](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-026.md), which checked the formulas against page renders. The formula (Eq. 11) is Forman's (2003) Bochner–Weitzenböck curvature specialised to a 1-dimensional complex by dropping the parent terms; the unit-weight form is [NOTE-026](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-026.md)'s substitution, not stated in the paper. The paper's applications (an EMD distance between curvature distributions, a Ricci flow for change detection, a Laplacian flow for denoising) are one-table or one-figure demonstrations, and several of its formulas carry sign and consistency slips, so it is cited here for the definition only. | Active |
| [THEORY-503](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-503.md) | Truncated SVD is the best rank-r approximation | Eckart & Young (1936), [LIT-330](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-330.md), read in full in [NOTE-301](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-301.md), which checked the error bound. The argument is first-order stationarity on the orthogonal group plus two cited theorems (the SVD and a simultaneous-SVD criterion), and assumes a minimiser exists. Only the Frobenius norm and real matrices are covered. Uniqueness is of the approximating matrix, under a spectral gap, never of the factors; the paper's last section argues the canonic components cannot be read straightforwardly as psychological factors. | Active |
| [THEORY-509](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-509.md) | MoE gate symmetry is only expert permutation | Tran, Trinh, Bui & Nguyen (2025), [LIT-670](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-670.md), read in [NOTE-513](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-513.md). Softmax is invariant to a common shift of scores and the sum to the order of terms, so G(n) = ℝ^d × ℝ × S_n preserves the layer; Theorems 4.1–4.2 show that generically it is all of the gate's symmetry, for dense gating and for top-k with k ≥ 2 (top-1 has an extra scaling). Aligning expert order and then each expert's hidden units gives barriers of 0.0044–0.0066 between GPT-2 MoE layers fine-tuned from different seeds, against 0.14–0.86 without the order step. Every experiment shares and freezes the backbone around the inserted layer, so it is not evidence about independently trained MoE models. | Active |
| [THEORY-515](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-515.md) v2 | Joint-space Schrödinger bridges sample posteriors | Shi, De Bortoli, Deligiannidis & Doucet (2022), [LIT-776](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-776.md), read in [NOTE-589](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md). Propositions 1–3 are proofs, read for structure and not checked line by line. The empirical gains over the conditional score model hold at equal, small step counts on most but not all image metrics, and in Lorenz-63 filtering at 20 steps. That a long noising horizon is not what makes conditional diffusion correct is [NOTE-589](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md)'s interpretation, not something the paper tests. | Active |
| [THEORY-516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) | Base category, not global sections, fixes logic | Butterfield & Isham (1998), [LIT-381](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-381.md), read in full in [NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md): Theorem 4.1 proves that generalized FUNC is exactly naturality of ν : G → Ω, for any presheaf G of posets on any small category. In classical physics the value presheaf has a global section per microstate (3.6–3.7), yet the macrostate and microstate valuations are sieve-valued, and [NOTE-329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-329.md) shows excluded middle failing at a microstate. Isham & Butterfield (1999), [LIT-389](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-389.md) ([NOTE-334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-334.md)), adds that Ω is unique for a given topos and that a base with one arrow between any two objects gives two-valued logic. The choice of base, and so of the logic, remains free. | Active |
| [THEORY-519](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-519.md) | Backprop is a functor into learners | Fong, Spivak & Tuyéras (2017; LICS 2019), [LIT-827](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-827.md), read in full in [NOTE-625](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-625.md), which followed the chain-rule proof of Theorem A.1 line by line. Learners (P, I, U, r) form Learn (Prop. II.4); Theorem III.2 makes gradient descent with backpropagation a functor Para → Learn. Covered: fixed step size, one datum per update, deterministic updates, and errors with invertible ∂e/∂x, which excludes cross-entropy at 0 and 1. That learners cannot compose without a request is argued, not proved. Learn says how learners compose, not whether they learn. | Active |
| [THEORY-524](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-524.md) | Čech obstruction is exact on cyclic scenarios | Carù (2018), [LIT-280](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-280.md), read in [NOTE-253](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-253.md), and the same result republished as Thm IV.32 of Carù's 2019 thesis, [LIT-281](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-281.md), read in [NOTE-254](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-254.md). The cyclic theorem is proved and was confirmed on Hardy, on the (2,2,4) counterexample and on 659 random contextual cycle models. The failures beyond cycles (Prop 8.2 / IV.34, the §8 cover, Conjecture 9.1 / IV.41) are the readers' computations and a lifting lemma, not the author's. The joint models grow exponentially; nothing analyses the cost. | Active |
| [THEORY-526](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-526.md) v2 | Čech obstruction is sound but incomplete | Abramsky, Mansfield & Barbosa (2011), [LIT-277](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-277.md) ([NOTE-250](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-250.md)); Abramsky, Barbosa, Kishida, Lal & Mansfield (2015), [LIT-278](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-278.md) ([NOTE-251](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-251.md)); Carù (2017), [LIT-279](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-279.md) ([NOTE-252](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-252.md)). The criterion (Prop 4.2 / Prop 16) and the All-vs-Nothing theorem (Thm 21) are proved; the three failures are explicit models, which the readers re-computed exactly over ℤ and ℤ/2. Two steps are the readers': that the §8 cover and the (2,2,4) model admit no All-vs-Nothing argument over any ring, by Thm 21 read contrapositively. The witness is possibilistic, so it cannot grade anything below strong contextuality. | Active |
| [THEORY-530](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-530.md) | Numerical range bounds rational functions | Badea & Beckermann (2013), [LIT-011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-011.md), a handbook survey read in full in [NOTE-009](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-009.md). Example 107.2.5: σ(A) is K-spectral iff A is diagonalisable, with K ≤ cond(V). Fact 107.7.2: the closure of W(A) is completely K-spectral for every bounded A with a universal K ∈ [2, 11.08], and 2 suffices for 2×2. The chapter proves almost nothing itself; the numerical range result is cited to Crouzeix (2007). The bound 11.08 was the 2013 state; a later improvement to 1 + √2 is recalled in the reading but not verified. Whether the constant is 2 was open. | Active |
| [THEORY-544](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-544.md) | Segal condition makes types category-like | Riehl & Shulman (2017), [LIT-032](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-032.md), read in full in [NOTE-069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-069.md). The internal results of §§5–11 are proved: associativity from the Segal condition applied to A^2 (Prop. 5.9), inner 3-horns (Prop. 5.21), functoriality of every function (Prop. 6.1), the dependent Yoneda lemma (Thm 9.5), and uniqueness of left adjoints into a Segal type from a Rezk type (Thm 11.23). Segal and Rezk types match Segal and complete Segal spaces (Props A.21, A.25), but soundness of the type theory in bisimplicial sets is sketched and depends on an unproved initiality theorem. Coherence in all dimensions is conjectured, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-553](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-553.md) | Topos quantities take spread values, not reals | Döring & Isham, paper III (2007/8), [LIT-299](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-299.md) ([NOTE-290](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-290.md)), restated with additions in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). The Gel'fand transforms of daseinised operators grow as contexts shrink, so arrows into the constant presheaf ℝ are impossible (3.3–3.4). Each Â gives a natural transformation δ̆^o(A) : Σ → ℝ^⪰ (Thm 3.1), and Â ↦ δ̆^o(A) is injective, by de Groote's results. ℝ^⪰ is a monoid, not a group; differences need a group completion, whose global elements are the functions of bounded variation on the context poset. No choice among the candidate value objects is made, and the state-dependent reading of the spread is cited, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-559](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-559.md) | KS contradictions refute measurement identity | Dzhafarov & Kujala (2017), [LIT-836](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-836.md), read in full in [NOTE-623](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-623.md). The transitivity step is an elementary proof; the reading of the reductio is an argument that rests on it. It binds the random-variable representation only: the sheaf account keeps one variable per measurement and asks whether marginals glue, and a reader who holds that view is not bound by it. The paper also proves that a coupling of a binary connection is multimaximal iff adjacent pairs, ordered by their means, are maximally coupled (Theorem II.3). | Active |
| [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md) v3 | Diffusion maps can recover Laplace–Beltrami | Coifman et al. (2005), [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md), read in full in [NOTE-1441](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1441.md). The finite construction and its isometry are [THEORY-728](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md); the paper's own diffusion distance is the one ã^(m) induces, not the inverse-stationary-weighted one. Theorem 2.1 and the α-family are stated without proof; the companion ([LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md)) proves the α-family's limit, Active without boundary as [THEORY-744](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-744.md), and its heat-kernel step is [QUESTION-231](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-231.md). Self-adjointness comes from the kernel's symmetry, and "directed diffusion" is anisotropic, not a non-reversible chain. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-566](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-566.md) v3 | Hyperbolic nets curve only through biases | Ganea, Bécigneul & Hofmann (2018), [LIT-879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-879.md), read in [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md), which checked the closed forms numerically. Möbius layers are defined as exp₀ ∘ f ∘ log₀, so any composition of them is exp₀ ∘ (the Euclidean composition) ∘ log₀, as the paper notes; only the Möbius bias, which is parallel transport from the origin followed by the exponential map, and the hyperbolic logistic regression's distances to geodesic hyperplanes are not absorbed by the chart. The structural fact is proved; that the networks' gains, confined to a synthetic task and to separating WordNet subtrees in low-dimensional Poincaré embeddings, come from those two operations is this record's inference. [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md) filed no THEORY. | Active |
| [THEORY-568](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-568.md) v2 | RSI counts k-way redundancy k−1 times | Gutknecht et al. (2025), [LIT-042](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-042.md), read in full in [NOTE-045](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-045.md), with the combinatorial proofs of Props. 1–4 and 6 checked by hand. The averages need only the consistency equation and I(X;Y) > 0; reading them as average degrees, and the bounds of Appendix B, need non-negative atoms. Corollary 5 overstates Prop. 6 (⇔ for ⇐). The network results are on tiny quantised models evaluated on their own training sets, and are not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-574](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-574.md) | Width bound is metric, and doesn't entail routing | Li (2026), [LIT-376](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-376.md) (Local Urysohn Width, v1), [LIT-375](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-375.md) (Structural Learning Theory) and [LIT-374](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-374.md) (Structural Decoupling), read jointly in [NOTE-323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-323.md), [NOTE-324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-324.md) and [NOTE-322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-322.md). In repaired form the formal core holds: width is incomparable with the per-cell VC dimension, fewer cells than width give an error floor (under an assumption that states it), and discovering all basins costs Ω(w log w) samples. But local correctness is automatic on any connected patch, the bouquet lower bound is metric (the paper's Remark 8.11 concedes it), a global classifier has width 1 (Remark 3.4), and the additive Rademacher bound said to call for decoupled training holds for joint training too. | Active |
| [THEORY-576](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-576.md) | Bundled networks split Fiedler and spectral dims | Grimaldi, Villegas, Vezzani, Burioni, Cassi & Gabrielli (2025; PRE Letter 2026), [LIT-028](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-028.md), read in full with its SM in [NOTE-005](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-005.md), which re-derived the key steps and checked them numerically on the comb. λ_{n1} = ℓ^b_{n1}/N_f gives d_g = 2(d_f,f + d_f,b)/(d_f,f + 2d_f,b/d_g,b) in the base-controlled regime; d_s = d_s,f is earlier work by the same group. The comb has d_s = 1 and d_g = 4/3. Proved for one graph class only; the paper's composite finite-size scaling prefactors (SM Eqs. 25, 29) are wrong, and its "generic property of composite architectures" outruns the proof. | Active |
| [THEORY-584](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-584.md) | Fidelity is minimized Bhattacharyya overlap | Fuchs (1995), [LIT-018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-018.md), read in full in [NOTE-021](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-021.md). min over POVMs of Σ_b √(tr ρ0E_b)√(tr ρ1E_b) equals tr√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2}) (Eq. 3.28), attained in the eigenbasis of M = ρ1^{-1/2}√(ρ1^{1/2}ρ0ρ1^{1/2})ρ1^{-1/2} (Eq. 3.67), whose eigenvalues are √(tr ρ0E_b / tr ρ1E_b) (Eq. 3.92). Proved for invertible ρ1 with a separate support construction, in finite dimension. The fidelity is the unsquared one; Jozsa's is its square. The thesis says nothing about trace distance, and the analogous problems for Rényi overlaps and the quantum Chernoff bound are left open. | Active |
| [THEORY-585](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-585.md) v3 | Topos pull-backs fail for tensor composites | Döring & Isham, paper IV (2007/8), [LIT-310](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-310.md) ([NOTE-285](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-285.md)), restated in [LIT-378](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-378.md) §§11–13 ([NOTE-326](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-326.md)). Classical physics satisfies the translation condition (3.18) exactly. For quantum disjoint sums the pull-back of δ̆(A₁⊕A₂) is δ̆(A₁) (Lemma 4.2, 4.24; checked). For H₁⊗H₂ the pull-back gives δ(Â₁)_{V_W}⊗1̂ at each context W, which equals δ(Â₁⊗1̂)_W on contexts V₁⊗ℂ1̂. That it differs elsewhere, and that no operator realises it, are asserted. The rules are "partly experimental", and the trivial-system rule contradicts the series' own definition of contexts. | Active |
| [THEORY-592](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-592.md) | C*-algebras embed as Hilbert-space operators | Gelfand & Naimark (1943), [LIT-313](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-313.md), read in full in [NOTE-303](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-303.md). Theorem 1 embeds every normed *-ring in B(H) for a Hilbert space not assumed separable; Lemma 1 is the commutative case, resting on Gelfand's 1941 paper and Šilov's boundary. The paper never says "C*-algebra" or "GNS". It assumes two axioms it suspected redundant, and notes that a single norm identity may replace two others. It gives the object-level isomorphism R ≅ C(𝔐), not a categorical duality, and nothing on uniqueness or irreducibility of the representation. | Active |
| [THEORY-595](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-595.md) | Ultrafilter extension is Lindenbaum's lemma | Turner (preprint 2021, published 2025), [LIT-145](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-145.md), read in [NOTE-177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-177.md). An expository paper: "None of the results are novel" (p. 2). Maximal, prime and ultra filters coincide (Thm 2); every filter extends to an ultrafilter (Thm 3); Łoś's theorem (Thm 9); compactness (Thm 12). The results are standard and correct, though the write-up has slips. A filter is only finitely consistent, and that is the point. The pairings with Lindenbaum and Henkin are analogies, not reductions. | Active |
| [THEORY-604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md) v2 | Most dualities are adjunctions to an opposite | Corfield (2017), [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md), read in [NOTE-141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md). A short programmatic paper. That most dualities of interest are covered by constructions around adjunction is shown by worked exposition of standard cases, not proved. There is unlikely to be "a single monolithic account" (pp. 59–60). Reserving "duality" for structural reversal is a stated preference, and the verdicts on string dualities are a paragraph each. The proposal that philosophers of physics need homotopy type theory is an expectation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-618](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-618.md) | Hyperbolic neural geometry evidence is thin | Sharpee (2019), [LIT-875](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-875.md), read in [NOTE-670](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-670.md): a four-page programmatic review with no new result, whose reading filed no THEORY because its claims are conjectures. Filed here as Proposed because the record holds two tests of the conjecture, odour statistics ([LIT-872](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-872.md), [THEORY-191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-191.md)) and CA1 place-cell correlations ([LIT-876](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-876.md), [THEORY-192](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-192.md)), and no general statement. The Zipf step shows a shared exponential count of states, which any system with extensive entropy has, not a shared metric, and the rigidity argument for three dimensions cites Mostow's theorem, which concerns finite-volume manifolds and says nothing about noisy point clouds. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-619](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-619.md) | Coarse-graining is direct image of clopens | Butterfield & Isham (2001), "Topos Perspective on the Kochen-Specker Theorem: IV", [LIT-382](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-382.md), read in full in [NOTE-328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-328.md). §2.4 proves G ≅ CloΣ: restricting the characters of V₁ that make P̂ true gives exactly the characters of V₂ that make its coarse-graining true, via a cited state-extension theorem. Theorem 3.1 shows that any assignment defined by "support ≤ coarse-grained proposition", with supports forming a global element of G, is a sieve-valued valuation obeying FUNC; a state's supports qualify. Both theorems are close to definitional. Nothing here builds Heyting operations on clopen sub-objects. | Active |
| [THEORY-620](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-620.md) | Walsh functions behave like Fourier series | Walsh (1923), [LIT-300](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-300.md), read in full in [NOTE-281](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-281.md), with the explicit formula and the Lebesgue-constant recurrence checked for small n. Closure is inherited from Haar's system, to which Walsh's is related by an orthogonal change of basis within each dyadic level. Theorems II–X give the Fourier-like convergence theory. The paper never mentions groups or characters: that these functions are the characters of the Cantor group, and of the Boolean cube on n digits, is a later identification. | Active |
| [THEORY-629](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-629.md) v2 | Hilbert-space functionals are inner products | Adler (2021), [LIT-243](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-243.md), read in full in [NOTE-854](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-854.md): two complete proofs, by projection (Thm 3.5) and by an orthonormal basis (Thm 4.9), with completeness used once, in the projection theorem. Riesz (1907), [LIT-326](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-326.md), read in [NOTE-289](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-289.md), is the priority note: existence of k with U(f) = ∫ f k for continuous linear U on square-summable functions, stated without proof, uniqueness or norm. The theorem says nothing about kernels, factorisation or uniqueness of representations. Both readings advise citing a textbook for anything leaned on. | Active |
| [THEORY-642](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-642.md) | Two-level type theory is conservative over HoTT | Annenkov, Capriotti, Kraus & Sattler (2017; MSCS 2023), [LIT-095](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-095.md), whose §§1–3 were read in full in [NOTE-047](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-047.md), the reading of the nLab page it supersedes ([LIT-040](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-040.md)). Props 2.18–2.19 prove that inhabitation of inner types is reflected, through a presheaf model over any model of HoTT. Thm 2.20 proves that a fibrant-replacement former implies UIP for inner types. The conservativity is the weak, inhabitation-reflecting kind. Results that use the axioms relating the two levels' natural numbers, which untruncated semisimplicial types need, are not known to transfer. | Active |
| [THEORY-645](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-645.md) | Compact and discrete abelian groups are dual | Pontryagin (1934), [LIT-333](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-333.md), read in full in [NOTE-284](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-284.md). Theorem 5 and the First Fundamental Theorem give the duality between countable discrete and compact second-countable abelian groups, with characters valued in ℝ/ℤ. The compact half rests on Peter–Weyl with Haar measure, used to extract one-dimensional characters. The Second and Third Fundamental Theorems are structure theorems, not duality. Commutative only; for non-abelian groups the relevant object is Peter–Weyl, and characters are traces, not homomorphisms. General locally compact duality is van Kampen's (1935). | Active |
| [THEORY-652](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-652.md) | Semisimple algebras are sums of matrix algebras | Wedderburn (1908), [LIT-309](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-309.md), read in full in [NOTE-280](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-280.md). Thm 17 with Thm 10 gives the unique decomposition into simple algebras; Thms 20–22 build n² matrix units from primitive idempotents and give simple = primitive × full matrix algebra. Primitive here means one idempotent, which makes the factor a division algebra once semisimple (Thm 15). The field is arbitrary, which was the paper's novelty. That the centre is spanned by the block identities follows from Thm 23's corollary; the paper never says "centre". The general splitting of an algebra into nilpotent plus semisimple parts is claimed in the summary but proved only in special cases. | Active |
| [THEORY-654](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-654.md) | LQR has ≥60° margin, lost with observers | Başar, Meyn & Perkins (2020), [LIT-051](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-051.md), graduate course notes read in full in [NOTE-062](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-062.md), with every worked example recomputed. §10.6 derives \|1 + L(jω)\|² = 1 + \|P(jω)\|²/r ≥ 1 for the full-state loop, hence \|S\| ≤ 1 and the classical margins. The derivation is for one input; the multi-input version needs more, which the notes do not discuss. The Pendubot thread shows a controllable, observable plant whose one-sensor observer-based design has gain margin below 10⁻². The result is Kalman's and standard; the notes are an adequate free citation for it. | Active |
| [THEORY-664](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-664.md) | Steering gives weak, not strong, self-duality | Barnum, Gaebler & Wilce (2009), [LIT-081](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-081.md), read in full in [NOTE-082](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-082.md). With matching dimensions a steering state is an order-isomorphism, and a cone is homogeneous iff every interior state purifies to an isomorphism state (Thm 4.1). Hence universal self-steering gives homogeneity and weak self-duality (Prop. 5.8). The weaker Prop. 5.7 is thinly argued. The C*-algebraic conclusion of §6 needs strong self-duality, which the paper assumes rather than derives. | Active |
| [THEORY-685](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-685.md) | Mizohata–Takeuchi conjecture is false | Cairo (2025), [LIT-030](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-030.md), read in full in [NOTE-051](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-051.md), which checked the counting and exponent bookkeeping. The paper states the theorem for any C² hypersurface not lying in a hyperplane; the proof needs a curved point, which a connected such surface has. The incidence lemma (§4) is the step a non-specialist could not verify. The loss is log R, not a power, and the counterexample is a family indexed by R. It does not refute endpoint multilinear restriction itself. Its proposed local replacement has since been refuted with power loss on a dense family of surfaces, per the abstract of a later paper. | Active |
| [THEORY-686](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-686.md) v2 | Join-preserving observations are left adjoints | Fong & Spivak (2018), [LIT-803](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-803.md), Chapter 1, read closely in a Skimmed NOTE ([NOTE-601](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-601.md)) whose other chapters were seen only at their openings. The results are standard order theory, re-derived by the record because NOTE-601 is a skim. The absence of generative effects is weaker than preserving all joins, and does not characterise the left adjoints. | Active |
| [THEORY-697](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-697.md) | Attention approximates SDM reads only locally | Bricken & Pehlevan (2021), [LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md), read in full in [NOTE-242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md), which re-evaluated the intersection formula and the fit. The intersection is a staircase in distance, the fit holds to about dv = 20 for d = 15, the analytic β of App. B.2 is about 2–2.5 times too small, and every optimal radius assumes random patterns and addresses. The GPT-2 "confirmation" and the cerebellar implementation of attention are argument, not demonstration. | Active |
| [THEORY-698](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-698.md) v2 | Probe lattices are guaranteed by construction | Xiong (2026), [LIT-267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-267.md), read in [NOTE-240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-240.md). Theorem 1 is the basic theorem of formal concept analysis applied to the crisp relation got by thresholding Fisher-LDA probes, and it holds for every binary relation; the paper's own proof plan says so. It is not evidence that language models encode a lattice beyond the incidence. | Active |
| [THEORY-713](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-713.md) | No three-source PID satisfies all axioms | Rauh, Bertschinger, Olbrich & Jost (2014), [LIT-1202](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1202.md), read in full in [NOTE-965](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-965.md). | [THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md) | More informative iff reproducible by garbling | Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), Theorems 4–6, read in [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md): the Sherman– Stein theorem, with a new minimax proof.
