| [THEORY-718](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-718.md) | Evidence is likelihood times an Occam factor | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), Eqs. 5–6 with Eqs. 16 and 19–20, read in [NOTE-471](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-471.md): for y = Φw + noise with Gaussian noise of precision β and the prior w ~ N(0, α⁻¹I) on k weights, the posterior is exactly Gaussian, so the evidence is exactly P(D\|w_MP) times the Occam factor P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A, with A = αI + βΦᵀΦ. If ΦᵀΦ/n converges to a positive-definite matrix and w_MP stays bounded, the log Occam factor is −(k/2) log n + O(1). Exact for this model class only. The general regular case and the singular case are [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md), which is Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md) v2 | Two contrastive losses share a density-ratio min | Johnson, El Hanchi & Maddison (2023), [LIT-258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md), App. B.2–B.3, read in [NOTE-751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-751.md): on a finite augmentation space, with every function of the two views allowed, the spectral contrastive loss is minimized by K⁺ = p⁺/(p⊗p) exactly, and the NT-Logistic loss with equal positive and negative classes by the log-odds log K⁺, so its exponentiated score is K⁺. Population optima over unconstrained functions only; not what an encoder reaches, and not InfoNCE, which is [THEORY-001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md)'s open part. | Active |
| [THEORY-720](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-720.md) | Cover-changing simulations add no contextuality | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md), Theorems 4.1, 4.3 and 4.5, read in [NOTE-651](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-651.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md), Theorems 21 and 22, read in [NOTE-647](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-647.md). A classical simulation answers each measurement of the target by a jointly measurable set of the source's, with shared classical randomness, so the cover may change. Non-contextual models are exactly those the empty model simulates, NCF cannot fall along a simulation, strong contextuality is reflected backwards, and a model clones itself only if it is non-contextual. No-signalling models on finite scenarios only. Which maps are simulations is [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md)'s open half. | Active |
| [THEORY-721](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-721.md) | †-Frobenius algebras are orthonormal bases | Three results [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) rested on, held apart from its synthesis. (a) The unitary group acts transitively on the orthonormal bases of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and on its tensor factorisations of given dimensions, so neither is fixed by the space; a non-degenerate self-adjoint operator fixes a basis up to phases, and its invariant content is its spectrum. (b) Over ℂ, commutative special †-Frobenius algebras correspond exactly to orthonormal bases: Coecke, Pavlovic & Vicary, [LIT-274](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-274.md), Thm 5.1 and §6, in finite dimension; Abramsky & Heunen, [LIT-275](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-275.md), Thm 22, for the non-unital ones satisfying the H*-axiom, in any dimension. (c) Over ℝ it fails: ℂ as a real algebra, with multiplication scaled by 1/√2, is a commutative special †-Frobenius algebra with no nonzero copyable vector. | Active |
| [THEORY-722](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-722.md) | CbD 2.0 contextuality depends on representation | Dzhafarov & Kujala (2017), [LIT-831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-831.md), Examples 1–3 and Section 4, read in [NOTE-643](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-643.md) (claims C4 and C6). Under multimaximal couplings, lumping values of non-binary variables can destroy every multimaximal coupling, so a noncontextual system becomes contextual. The verdict on a fixed set of measurements therefore depends on which variables represent them. For connections of two variables, hence cyclic systems, and for consistently connected systems, the 1.0 and 2.0 definitions agree. It does not say the coupling choice changes verdicts in larger connections, which is [THEORY-168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md)'s asserted part. | Active |
| [THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md) | Softmax fixes representations up to linear map | Nielsen et al. (2025), [LIT-253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-253.md), read in full in [NOTE-738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-738.md), with Harvey, Larsen & Williams (2023), [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md), for the kernel side. What is observed fixes a representation only up to that observation's symmetry group: a centred linear kernel up to a translation and an orthogonal map ([THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)), and a softmax output distribution up to an invertible linear map of the embedding with the inverse transpose on the unembedding (Thm 2.2). KL can go to zero while the embeddings stay non-linearly related (Thm 3.1, Cor. 3.2), but d_LLV ≤ ε gives d_f,g ≤ 2Mε (Thm 4.7). Final layer only. It does not say what the Platonic hypothesis means; that is [THEORY-002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-724](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-724.md) v2 | Destabilization by switching needs non-normality | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), Part II, [LIT-929](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-929.md), eq. 12 and §4, read in [NOTE-842](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-842.md). Because d‖u‖²/dt = u†(A + A†)u, the first Lyapunov exponent lies between the long-run averages of the extreme eigenvalues of the Hermitian part. For a normal operator the largest is the spectral abscissa, so an operator that is normal and uniformly stable at every instant has a negative exponent. A switched undamped oscillator, neutral at every instant, has a positive exponent. The stochastic genericity results are [THEORY-325](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-325.md)'s, still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) | Weight decay on factors is nuclear-norm penalty | Boncoraglio et al. (2025), [LIT-857](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-857.md), Appendix A, read in [NOTE-661](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-661.md), and re-derived here. ‖W‖²_F = Tr(WWᵀ) = ‖WWᵀ‖_*, since a PSD matrix's singular values are its eigenvalues. For untied factors, Hölder's inequality for Schatten norms and AM–GM bound ‖M‖_* by (‖U‖²_F + ‖V‖²_F)/2 over every factorization UVᵀ = M, and the balanced SVD factorization attains it. The product's rank is bounded by the factors' inner dimension. It says nothing about what the trained product looks like, which is [THEORY-180](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-180.md)'s spectral law. | Active |
| [THEORY-727](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-727.md) v2 | Transient growth exceeds what eigenvalues show | Farrell & Ioannou (1996), [LIT-931](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-931.md), read in [NOTE-831](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-831.md), with Trefethen et al. (1993), [LIT-932](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-932.md), read in [NOTE-839](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-839.md). For du/dt = Au with A fixed: a normal A grows as its spectral abscissa; in general the growth over t is σ_max(e^(At)), with the eigenvalues as a floor; the initial growth rate is the top eigenvalue of (A + A†)/2; and harmonic forcing is bounded by κ(E)/dist(iω, Λ(A)), with the ε-pseudospectrum marking where eigenvalues of A + Δ, ‖Δ‖ < ε, can go. All in a chosen norm. The white-noise variance result is [THEORY-323](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-323.md)'s, still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-728](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md) v2 | Finite diffusion maps preserve diffusion distance | Coifman et al. (2005), LIT-981, read in full in NOTE-1441, with the derivation written out here; the 1/π-weighted distance is the companion's (LIT-1246), not the paper's own. For n points and a symmetric affinity K with positive entries, A = D⁻¹K is a Markov matrix with stationary law π ∝ d. It is conjugate to the symmetric D^(-1/2) K D^(-1/2), so its eigenvalues are real and in [−1, 1], and in [0, 1] when K is positive semi-definite. The map x ↦ (λ_j^m ψ_j(x))_{j≥1} turns the m-step diffusion distance, weighted by 1/π, into Euclidean distance exactly. Truncation gives a lower bound. It says nothing about the continuum limit, which is [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-729](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-729.md) | Adjunctions restrict to dual equivalences | Corfield (2017), [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md), §3, read in full in [NOTE-141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md), with the proof the paper omits written out here. For F : C → D^op left adjoint to G : D^op → C, let C′ and D′ be the full subcategories on which the unit and the counit are isomorphisms. Then F and G restrict to inverse equivalences C′ ≃ D′, and D′ is a full subcategory of D^op, so C′ is dually equivalent to a full subcategory of D. Pontrjagin duality is the example. That most dualities are of this form is [THEORY-604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md)'s thesis, still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-730](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-730.md) v2 | Lattice co-occurrence gives Fourier embeddings | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart & Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md), Propositions 1, 3 and 4 and Corollary 2, with the proofs in Appendix E followed in [NOTE-664](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-664.md). The result is conditional throughout. It concerns an idealised embedding with W Wᵀ = \|M*\| and d ≥ rank M*, not a trained one. It needs the positive and negative parts of M* to be translation invariant separately (Assumption B.1), not M* alone. It says nothing about whether any corpus or model satisfies these conditions, which is [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-731](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-731.md) | Class-centre term floors Gauss–Newton spectrum | Papyan (2019), [LIT-619](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-619.md), read in [NOTE-479](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-479.md). Exact algebra, re-derived here. For softmax cross-entropy, the Gauss–Newton matrix is G = (1/n)ΔΔᵀ, an uncentred second moment of logit derivatives indexed by class and logit. Grouping them gives G = G₀ + G₁ + G₂ + G₃, with every term positive semidefinite. G₁, the class-centre term, has rank at most C, and its spectrum is read from a C × C Gram matrix. So λ_k(G) ≥ λ_k(G₁ + G₂) ≥ λ_k(G₁) for every k, in any network, trained or not. That G₁ carries the outliers of trained networks is measured, not derived, and stays Proposed in [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-733](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-733.md) v2 | Exact dynamical independence is non-generic | Barnett and Seth (2023), [LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md), read in [NOTE-791](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-791.md): the VAR form (3.26) of exact dynamical independence, with the genericity count of §3.3 made a proof for VAR order p ≥ 2 and corrected for p = 1. Linear coarse-grainings Y = LX of a stable VAR with non-degenerate Gaussian innovations only. It says nothing about near-independence, about the multimodality of the dynamical-dependence cost, or about nonlinear maps. | Active |
| [THEORY-734](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-734.md) v2 | Hyperbolic trees need many bits of precision | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md), Lemma D.1, read in [NOTE-679](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-679.md), with the proof redone here without the paper's small-angle approximation. Only the root's children are used to fix the embedding's scale c, and then the chains turn the scale into depth. Plane only, one family of trees, fixed-point coordinates in the Poincaré disk, deg_max ≥ 15 and ε ≤ 1. It says nothing about H^r for r > 2, or about whether any tree needs fewer bits under another number system. | Active |
| [THEORY-735](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-735.md) | Batch size trades steps against examples | McCandlish, Kaplan, Amodei et al. (2018), [LIT-348](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-348.md), §2 and App. D.1, as read and re-derived in [NOTE-293](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-293.md). A derivation under stated assumptions: a second-order model of the loss along the step, an unbiased minibatch gradient of covariance Σ/B, and the step size that maximises the expected decrease. It says nothing about whether real training meets those assumptions, or how well the noise scale predicts the measured critical batch, which is [THEORY-033](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-033.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-736](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-736.md) v2 | Dropout-stable solutions are mode connected | Kuditipudi et al. (2019), [LIT-671](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-671.md), Theorem 1, read in full in [NOTE-544](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-544.md), with Draxler et al.'s (2018) concatenation bound from [LIT-653](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-653.md). Dropout stability gives every solution a half-width copy with the same loss up to ε. Half the units are then free, so working units can be swapped in and permuted at no cost. That joins any two such solutions. It is a statement about dropout-stable solutions only: whether training produces them is [THEORY-109](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-109.md)'s open question, and Theorem 4 of the same paper builds disconnected global minima. | Active |
| [THEORY-738](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-738.md) v2 | Imbalanced max-margin optimum is simplex labels | Thrampoulidis, Kini, Vakilian and Behnia (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), Theorem 1 and Corollary 1.3, read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) and re-derived here. By [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) the problem is nuclear-norm minimisation of the logits under margin constraints. The polar factor of the simplex-encoded label matrix certifies it optimal, because under step imbalance its off-diagonal entries are negative. It does not say that gradient descent or trained networks reach this geometry, which is [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-739](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-739.md) v2 | word2vec proxy learns eigenvectors in sequence | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md), Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, read in [NOTE-660](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-660.md) and re-derived here. The quartic proxy is a function of WWᵀ alone, so von Neumann's trace inequality gives its rank-d minimisers. Gradient flow from an aligned start keeps the eigenbasis and reduces each mode to a logistic equation. It does not say that word2vec, or the proxy from random initialisation, behaves this way; that is [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-740](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-740.md) v2 | Deep linear nets learn modes one at a time | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014, 2019), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md) and [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md) and [NOTE-666](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-666.md), re-derived here. From a decoupled, balanced start the two-layer equations keep the SVD basis of Σyx, and each mode's strength obeys τȧ = 2a(s − a), a logistic rise. One weight matrix on the same data relaxes every mode exponentially on the one timescale τ. It does not say that random starts follow the solution, which is [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-741](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-741.md) | Wide nets' global minima share a linked minimum | Lin, Li and Wu (2024), [LIT-682](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-682.md), Theorems 6, 11 and 18 with Lemmas 7 and 25, read in [NOTE-535](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-535.md) and re-derived by the promotion audit. Two toy models whose minima can be written down: a two-layer ReLU student of an orthonormal teacher on the sphere at population loss, and a deep linear network fitting y = Qx. Spare width lets every minimum be moved, along segments of minima, to one a common centre can reach. No permutation symmetry is used, and nothing is claimed about trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-744](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-744.md) v3 | α sets the limit diffusion's invariant density | Coifman and Lafon (2006), [LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), read in [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md), with the PNAS announcement [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md). The paper states the limit as a Schrödinger operator. Written as a drift, it shows what each α keeps of the density: the walk's stationary density is q^{2(1−α)}. On a manifold without boundary the limit is derived in full, the kernel expansion included (re-derived on promotion, 2026-10-20). The paper's own α = 1/2 display has a sign error. Its boundary rate and heat-kernel proof are incomplete and are left to [QUESTION-231](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-231.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-745](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-745.md) | Diffusion-map truncation error is absolute | Coifman and Lafon (2006), [LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), read in full in [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md). The identity D_t² = Σ λ_l^{2t}(ψ_l(x) − ψ_l(y))² is exact. The paper's Proposition 1 says the truncated map keeps it "up to relative accuracy δ". The true bound is absolute and can be large relative to D_t for nearby points. In the refinement sense, the diffusion-map family coarsens with t only through the threshold. Finite sets, counting measure and reversible walks only. It says nothing about the manifold limit or about non-reversible chains. | Active |
| [THEORY-746](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-746.md) | Slow feature analysis is an eigenproblem | Wiskott and Sejnowski (2002), [LIT-1249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1249.md), read in full in [NOTE-971](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-971.md). Within the span of a fixed basis, the slowest decorrelated unit-variance outputs are the bottom generalized eigenvectors of the pencil (⟨ż̃ż̃ᵀ⟩, cov z̃), and each output's slowness is its eigenvalue. A consequence the paper does not draw: a stack of such stages whose function spaces contain their inputs is never faster at a higher stage, componentwise, on the training signal, so in this model "higher is slower" is imposed by the objective, weakly, and can stall. It is about the training signal and a fixed function space. It says nothing about test data, about a generative model, about invariance as opposed to slowness, or about learning dynamics. | Active |
| [THEORY-747](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-747.md) | Finite-memory MZ closure rivals Smagorinsky | Parish and Duraisamy (2017), [LIT-1259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1259.md), read in [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md). The closure is [THEORY-760](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md)'s finite Markovian augmentation. Here is how it did, as far as the paper's plots show: close to filtered DNS in integral quantities, comparable to dynamic Smagorinsky in equilibrium turbulence, clearly better on a transitional flow, and with the subgrid transfer peaked at the cutoff where DNS puts it but about 40% too deep. The paper calls the predictions "excellent" with no numbers. Its fitted memory length shortens as the resolved dynamics speed up, so the memory belongs to the cutoff as much as to the flow. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md) v4 | Euler solutions above 1/3 conserve energy | Constantin, E and Titi (1994), [LIT-1248](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1248.md), read in [NOTE-982](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-982.md). The positive half of Onsager's conjecture, in the Besov form: if velocity increments obey ‖u(·+y) − u‖_{L³} ≤ C\|y\|^α with α > 1/3, integrated in time, the coarse-grained energy flux across scale ε is O(ε^(3α−1)) and no energy can be lost to vanishing scales. It is a statement about regular fields only. It does not show that a flux survives the limit for rougher ones: that energy can fail to be conserved below 1/3 is Isett's later theorem ([THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md)), that it can strictly decrease is Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol's (THEORY-776), both Proposed, and some rough solutions conserve energy anyway. | Active |
| [THEORY-751](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-751.md) v2 | Refinability needs a Markov chain of channels | Equitz and Cover (1991), [LIT-1238](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1238.md), read in [NOTE-988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-988.md), with every step re-derived by 2026-10-20. Lossless two-stage description is possible exactly when the coarse optimum is a stochastic degradation of the fine optimum. That is a Markov chain on test channels, not nesting of partitions, and it is an asymptotic block-coding statement. It does not say that optimal single-shot quantizers or deterministic encoders nest, and the paper's own Gaussian example shows they need not. It says nothing yet about the information bottleneck beyond a formal transfer through the KL distortion. | Active |
| [THEORY-752](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-752.md) | t-model memory acts as growing damping | Chorin, Hald and Kupferman (2002), [LIT-1253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1253.md), read in [NOTE-975](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-975.md): Theorem 8.1. Truncating the Mori–Zwanzig memory integral at its lag-zero value gives dΦ/dt = R̄(Φ) + tS(Φ), and under the stated conditions this dissipates the free energy of the resolved variables. It says nothing about how well the t-model predicts, gives no error bound, and holds only for the conditional-expectation projection; the true conditional mean's effective energy need not decrease. | Active |
| [THEORY-753](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-753.md) | IB refinability is a convex-hull test | Charvin, Catenacci Volpi and Polani (2023), [LIT-1258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1258.md), read in [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md). It turns [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md)'s Markov formulation into a finite check: nesting between two IB optima is a convex-hull inclusion of their decoder points, which a linear programme decides. The check is on given optima, and refinability asks for some pair. So a failed check settles the question only when the optima are certified globally optimal and unique. This entry adds that the information bottleneck's own convex-envelope dual can supply that certificate. Finite alphabets, two stages. | Active |
| [THEORY-754](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-754.md) v3 | Energy transfer is local in scale | Eyink and Aluie (2009), [LIT-1239](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1239.md), read in [NOTE-969](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-969.md), stating bounds proved in Eyink (2005), [LIT-1252](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1252.md). A conditional inequality: if velocity increments scale no faster than r^σ in the L³ mean, the contributions of far larger and far smaller scales to the mean flux across ℓ are bounded by powers of the scale ratio. It needs 0 < σ < 1: σ < 1 for the large scales, σ > 0 for the small. That the inertial range satisfies the hypothesis, that the mean flux there is non-zero, and the sharper 4/3 exponent are assumptions or heuristics, not part of it. It is about one field decomposed by scale, and says nothing about units. | Active |
| [THEORY-755](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-755.md) v3 | Exact aggregation needs column-equitability | Shpak, Stadler, Wagner and Hermisson (2004), [LIT-1242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1242.md), read in [NOTE-979](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-979.md). Exact aggregation of a linear system by the sums over a partition holds for every state iff the partition is column-equitable, a symmetry condition, not a weak-coupling one. Linear dynamics and partition-based aggregation only. It says nothing about approximate aggregation, the Simon–Ando case, or nonlinear systems, where the paper itself shows aggregations with no linear counterpart. | Active |
| [THEORY-757](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-757.md) v2 | IB refinable when Y=f(X) or both binary | Charvin, Catenacci Volpi and Polani (2023), [LIT-1258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1258.md), read in [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md). These are the two finite cases in which nested information-bottleneck optima are guaranteed at every pair of budgets. Neither reaches the record's four-state source, whose Y is not a function of X and whose X has three effective states. [NOTE-981](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-981.md) finds that source not refinable. So binary Y alone does not guarantee nesting. The function case is the degenerate one, where the bottleneck is just a noisy copy of Y. | Active |
| [THEORY-758](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-758.md) v3 | Diffusion-wavelet levels are spectral bands | Coifman and Maggioni (2006), [LIT-1256](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1256.md), read in full in [NOTE-984](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-984.md). The levels of a diffusion multiresolution are spectral bands. Nesting is exact and needs no decay of the spectrum, and decay buys only compression. The compressed algorithm as written keeps ⟨ξ : λ^{2^{j−1}} > ε⟩ at level j, and the paper's own Fig. 9 follows this, not its stated count. Each level closes exactly under T, but a single scaling function does not. It says nothing about non-self-adjoint operators, about error bounds for the compressed scheme with finite precision, or about when a localized basis exists. | Active |
| [THEORY-760](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-760.md) | Finite-memory MZ closure is Markovian, inexact | Parish and Duraisamy (2017), [LIT-1259](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1259.md), read in [NOTE-973](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-973.md). The finite-memory closure turns the Mori–Zwanzig memory integral into auxiliary ordinary differential equations, so the reduced model is the resolved variables plus finitely many memory coordinates: the shape of augmentation [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) asks about. But the truncation drops the next auxiliary term without a bound, the memory length is fitted, and the kernel's form is fixed by the quadrature, not by the eliminated dynamics. It is an augmentation with uncontrolled error, not the controlled one the question asks for. | Active |
| [THEORY-761](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-761.md) v2 | Piecewise-linear Fourier decay is k^(−d−1) | Rahaman et al. (2019), [LIT-1261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1261.md), read in full in [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md). One integration by parts turns f̃ into a sum of polytope transforms weighted by the region gradients and divided by k. Each further step of Diaz et al.'s recursion gains another 1/k until the path reaches a face whose directions are all orthogonal to k. Generic directions reach the vertices, giving k^(−d−1), and every direction gets at least k^(−2). It is a bound on what a piecewise-linear function contains, not a statement about training. Unbounded ReLU networks fall outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-762](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-762.md) | Eigenfunctions are memoryless in mean only | The record's answer to what Nadler et al. ([LIT-1250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1250.md), read in [NOTE-986](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-986.md)) leave implicit when they call slow eigenfunctions reaction coordinates. Such a coordinate is exactly closed in its mean: its best prediction from the full state and from its own history coincide, with no memory term, and the Mori–Zwanzig memory and noise for it vanish under Mori's projection. It is closed in law only under a further condition. In the paper's examples the condition holds; the mixed Ornstein–Uhlenbeck eigenfunction x₁x₂ shows it can fail. This does not say that diffusion maps estimate the eigenfunctions well from finite data, or that a slow eigenfunction is the best coarse variable. | Active |
| [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) v2 | Euler solutions below 1/3 can dissipate | Isett (2018), [LIT-1255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1255.md), skimmed in [NOTE-974](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-974.md): the negative half of Onsager's conjecture. With [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md) (Constantin, E and Titi, the positive half) it makes 1/3 the threshold. For the record, its point is that below 1/3 the energy flux into vanishing scales can survive the limit, which is the half of A3's point that THEORY-749 could not give. It does not say that this flux is a dissipative cascade. Isett's solutions start from rest, gain energy and lose it again, so the surviving flux takes both signs. Nor does it say that such solutions are limits of Navier–Stokes or describe turbulence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-770](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-770.md) v2 | Price equation needs only population closure | Luque (2016), [LIT-205](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-205.md), §3, read in [NOTE-101](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-101.md), after Price (1970); the derivation re-derived by the promotion audit. An identity, not a model: it says nothing about which partition of the change a causal model licenses, predicts nothing until fitness and transmission are specified, and fails without closure (migration). | Active |
| [THEORY-771](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-771.md) v5 | Below ε_c, contracting slow–fast stays O(ε) close | Bousquet and Slotine (arXiv 2015), [LIT-1292](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1292.md), read in [NOTE-1025](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1025.md). It gives Simon's near-decomposability the rate in ε that [THEORY-661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md)'s open statement lacks: first order, for trajectory error, uniform in time, under contraction of the modules and of the reduced slow system, with an explicit, sufficient ceiling on ε. Deterministic. It bounds how far the states are from the reduced description, not how much information the rest of the system sends into the slow variables, and it takes the slow coordinates as given. | Active |
| [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md) v2 | Euler solutions can confine dissipation to pipes | Giri, Kwon and Novack (2023; Annals 2026), [LIT-1289](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1289.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1022](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1022.md): the L³-based strong Onsager theorem. Below 1/3, in Constantin, E and Titi's own scale of spaces ([THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)), there are weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality. In the proof the Duchon–Robert measure is a prescribed smooth function, positive in a periodic array of pipes and zero elsewhere. So the coarse-grained flux into vanishing scales is one-signed locally in space and time, in the limit, and not only for the whole box as in [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md). Its location and rate are inputs of the construction; it is a smooth density on a few pipes, not concentrated on a thin set; nothing is said about the sign at a positive scale or about vanishing viscosity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-773](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md) v2 | Slow-manifold error is O(ε) under contraction | Del Vecchio and Slotine (IEEE TAC 2013), [LIT-1295](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1295.md), read in [NOTE-1020](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1020.md), with their Theorem 3's hypothesis corrected. A global, uniform-in-time, first-order bound on the error of the quasi-steady-state reduction, with every constant explicit and no requirement that ε be small. The reduction is Markovian: eliminating a fast, contracting variable costs O(ε) in trajectory error for all time, so no memory term is needed to that order. Constant metrics, deterministic, and the bound d on how fast the manifold moves is needed along the trajectory. | Active |
| [THEORY-775](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-775.md) | VAE slowness prior gives SFA only when whitened | Schüler and Wiskott (2025), [LIT-1296](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1296.md), read in full in [NOTE-1015](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1015.md). The ELBO of a dynamical VAE with prior N(z_{t−1}, I) and encoder N(g(x_t), I) is Σ E log p(x_t \| z_t) − ½Σ‖g(x_{t−1}) − g(x_t)‖² − (T − 1)d/2, an exact identity. For linear Gaussian encoder and decoder on whitened input, the maximizer spans the bottom eigenvectors of the difference covariance with eigenvalue μ < 1, each scaled by (μ^{−1/2} − 1)^{1/2} and then rotated arbitrarily. So it recovers SFA's slow span, cut at lag-one autocorrelation ½, not SFA's features. On raw input it trades variance against slowness. It says nothing about nonlinear encoders, about predictive sufficiency, or about Turner and Sahani's model. | Active |
| [THEORY-776](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-776.md) v3 | Euler solutions can follow any decreasing energy | Buckmaster, De Lellis, Székelyhidi and Vicol (2017; CPAM 2019), [LIT-1300](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1300.md), read in [NOTE-1013](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1013.md): the admissible version of Isett's negative half of Onsager's conjecture ([THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md)). Any smooth positive energy profile can be imposed on a C^β solution, β < 1/3, so a strictly decreasing one gives solutions whose total energy only falls. Through [THEORY-749](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-749.md)'s energy balance, the coarse-grained flux then runs into the vanishing scales on every time interval. That is the one-way transfer [THEORY-763](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-763.md) could not give. It is one-way for the box as a whole, not at every point (no local energy inequality is proved); the same theorem gives increasing energy as readily, so the direction is a choice of the construction; and nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes, to a constant-flux inertial range or to uniqueness. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-811](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-811.md) | Kernel quantum entropy approximates KL to O(σ²) | The general reading that [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one kernel family on the torus that the rate is shown for. Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md), asserts that other translation-invariant kernels and kernels on compact groups behave alike, and sketches a leverage-score argument without completing it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-812](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-812.md) | ℓ₁ phase transition is universal across ensembles | The general reading that [THEORY-391](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-391.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to what 2,948,000 optimizations at three problem sizes showed. Donoho and Tanner (2009), [LIT-1160](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1160.md), read in [NOTE-933](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-933.md), state it as the hypothesis of "weak universality" and pose the class of ensembles it holds for as an open problem. Nothing about non-Gaussian ensembles is proved. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-819](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-819.md) | Wiener projection removes Mori–Zwanzig memory | Lin and Lu (2021), [LIT-1307](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1307.md), read in [NOTE-1029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1029.md). Mori–Zwanzig's memory is what a projection onto the present leaves out; a projection onto the whole past absorbs it, leaving the causal Wiener filter on the coarse variable's own history and a residual orthogonal to all of that history. Second-order (linear-span) projections, invertible dynamics and stationarity only. It gives no finite augmentation with a bounded error in general: the NARMAX step is the paper's uncontrolled approximation, exact only in the linear Gaussian class shown here. | Active |
| [THEORY-820](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-820.md) v2 | Informational closure equals causal closure | Rosas et al. (arXiv 2024), [LIT-1306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1306.md), read in [NOTE-1030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1030.md), with Barnett and Seth's definition ([LIT-979](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-979.md)). For discrete stationary processes, the information-theoretic criterion of emergent closure (dynamical independence), the interventionist one (the macro's own causal states are all the micro distinctions that matter for it) and, for maps of the present state, a computational one are nested as stated. The first two are one condition. It says nothing about approximate closure. It does not make closure a mark of unity. "Causal" is only in the Granger sense unless X is fully observed. | Active |
| [THEORY-821](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-821.md) | Locally dissipative Euler solutions exist, α<1/15 | Isett (2017; ARMA 2022), [LIT-1305](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1305.md), skimmed in [NOTE-1027](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1027.md): the first continuous, indeed C^α with α < 1/15, weak Euler solutions satisfying the local energy inequality with nonzero dissipation, and a Cantor family of them sharing one initial datum and one dissipation measure. In the construction the dissipation measure is a function of time alone, so in the limit of vanishing scale the energy flux runs one way at every place, as in [THEORY-772](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-772.md), but in a Hölder class and spread uniformly over the torus rather than set in pipes. It is switched on only while the constructor drains the solution's energy to zero at the end of its life. Where, when and how fast the energy goes are inputs; the exponent is far from 1/3; nothing ties these solutions to Navier–Stokes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-822](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-822.md) v2 | Strong lumpability gives informational closure | Rosas et al. (arXiv 2024), [LIT-1306](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1306.md), read in [NOTE-1030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1030.md), on Kemeny–Snell lumpability, joined to Shpak et al.'s column-equitable partitions ([LIT-1242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1242.md), [THEORY-755](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-755.md)). Exact closure of a block label in a Markov chain is a condition on transition rows, a symmetry, and not weak coupling. The converse needs the label to be Markov: a closed label can have memory. Exact results only, with no bound for nearly lumpable partitions. | Active |
| [THEORY-829](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-829.md) | Ultralarge conjunctions of beliefs can fail | Wenmackers (2011), [LIT-163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-163.md), Ch. 3 (Stratified Belief, Def. 1; the Stratified Conjunction Principle, Def. 2, eq. 3.5 and §3.6.3.2), read in full in [NOTE-139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md); re-derived by the promotion audit from finite subadditivity and Hrbacek's Closure principle. A result inside the framework: it says nothing about whether belief has levels, and any explicit level boundary collapses the model back to a fixed threshold. | Active |
| [THEORY-847](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-847.md) | Block averaging exact iff columns sum equally | Rubenstein et al. (2017), [LIT-1334](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1334.md), read in [NOTE-1037](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1037.md), with Beckers and Halpern's restatement ([LIT-1316](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1316.md), Example 3.3). Averages of linear micro-variables form a causally consistent macro model exactly when each micro-cause has the same total effect on the effect block. It says nothing about interventions on single micro-variables, which break exactness, nor about nonlinear or approximate aggregation. | Active |
| [THEORY-875](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-875.md) | Phenomenal binding modelled as a sheaf condition | Lee-Youngzie, Tsuchiya, Robinson, Dietz & Monti (2026), [LIT-1352](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1352.md), read in full in [NOTE-1059](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1059.md). A hypothesis article with no data. It proposes the presheaf and two readings of its failure, disunity for rivalry and context dependence for the Ebbinghaus illusion, without a criterion between them. It does not identify unity with a global section, since it assumes unity always holds. Its global section is measured data, its worked topology example is malformed, and by its own definition of gluing the rivalry case is not a sheaf failure. It answers [QUESTION-255](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-255.md) only by showing that a sheaf failure need not be disunity. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-894](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-894.md) v2 | Every finite game is potential plus harmonic | Jiang, Lim, Yao & Ye (2011), [LIT-1439](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1439.md), Theorems 4.7, 4.8 and 5.1: the Hodge/Helmholtz decomposition of edge flows, and HodgeRank's least-squares ranking with its curl and harmonic residuals. Candogan, Menache, Ozdaglar & Parrilo (2011), [LIT-1442](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1442.md), Theorems 4.1 and 5.1: every finite game is P ⊕ H ⊕ N, and potential games are P ⊕ N. Both read from arXiv; the proofs were followed. Settled as mathematics. Whether its shares measure a negotiation's potential depends on cardinal assumptions that the record's orderings do not supply. | Active |
| [THEORY-896](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-896.md) v4 | Finite improvement iff ordinal potential exists | Monderer and Shapley (1996), [LIT-1462](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1462.md), unread: reported by Duersch, Oechssler and Schipper (arXiv 1003.4274) as Lemma 2.5. A finite game has the finite improvement property iff it has a generalized ordinal potential. The record proves the finite case here: a potential that rises with every improvement forbids cycles, and an acyclic improvement graph on finitely many profiles has an integer potential, the length of the longest improvement path into each profile. It is the precise form of "an ordering prevails" ⇔ "no improvement cycles", and it is ordinal. | Active |
| [THEORY-916](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-916.md) v2 | Influence power accumulates by centrality | Jia, MirTabatabaei, Friedkin & Bullo (2015), [LIT-1146](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1146.md), read in [NOTE-1135](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1135.md) from the version of record posted on the author's site; proofs skimmed. Theorems about a model, not findings about groups. The empirical companion, [LIT-1482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1482.md) ([THEORY-902](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-902.md)), uses anchored dynamics and a changing network, whose attractor is autocracy rather than this interior equilibrium. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-924](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-924.md) v3 | Elo fits exactly only acyclic log-odds | Balduzzi et al. (2018), [LIT-1508](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1508.md), Propositions 1 and 3 and appendix A, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1155](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1155.md), proofs followed. When the log-odds are curl-free, Elo ratings are their row means; otherwise batch Elo's fixed point matches only row sums and differs from the row means. Elo fits exactly iff log-odds sum to zero around every triangle, so it has no predictive power in rock-paper-scissors, and duplicating an agent moves the ratings of agents that beat or lose to it. Cardinal throughout. | Active |
| [THEORY-926](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-926.md) v3 | n bits realize any antisymmetric win pattern | Czarnecki et al. (2020), [LIT-1504](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1504.md), Theorem 1 and Propositions 1–2, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md), proof followed. Strategies announce an identity, then throw or take the game as the pattern says. Go is at least about 1000-bit communicative (log₂ 180! ≈ 1094), so it has cycles of length 2¹⁰⁰⁰. Ordinal: only the sign of outcomes matters. The paper states it for patterns with draws too, which also needs a draw to stay attainable. The strategies are weak by construction. | Active |
| [THEORY-940](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-940.md) v3 | Nash clusters order by population performance | Czarnecki et al. (2020), [LIT-1504](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1504.md), Definition 3 and Theorems 2–3, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1146](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1146.md), proofs followed and re-derived. RPP is the population value of Balduzzi et al. (2019), [LIT-1509](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1509.md). It holds for any Nash clustering of any finite symmetric zero-sum game and does not depend on the spinning-top hypothesis. The order is weak, since clusters can tie, and cardinal, since RPP uses payoff magnitudes. | Active |
| [THEORY-944](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-944.md) v3 | Population Nash value is equilibrium-independent | Balduzzi et al. (2019), [LIT-1509](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1509.md), Propositions 2 and 5, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1143](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1143.md), proofs followed and re-derived. Relative population performance is a game value, so equilibrium selection never arises. Behaviourally redundant members leave it unchanged, and a population contained in another's behavioural hull cannot beat it. It scores populations, not members, it is cardinal, and populations not nested by hull can still beat one another in a cycle. | Active |
| [THEORY-946](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-946.md) v3 | Max-entropy Nash average ignores agent copies | Balduzzi et al. (2018), [LIT-1508](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1508.md), Proposition 4, Lemma 1 and Theorem 1, read from arXiv v2 in [NOTE-1155](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1155.md), proofs followed. The paper claims invariance to redundant copies without the uniqueness condition. Its proof covers the Nash set, not the maximum-entropy selection. A counterexample checked by script (one copy of a null agent moves an outside agent's Nash average from −0.5 to −0.2) shows the condition is needed. Cardinal: payoffs are log-odds. | Active |
| [THEORY-971](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-971.md) | Additive units cannot detect a given sum | Ameisen et al. (2025), [LIT-1552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1552.md), read in [NOTE-1185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1185.md), re-derived here. It is why their addition graphs contain "lookup table" features between operand features and sum features. Whether a given unit in a trained model meets the premise is an empirical matter: attention patterns that depend on both operands, or any earlier nonlinearity that mixes them, break it, and that mixing is exactly the intermediate step the result says is required. | Active |
| [THEORY-981](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-981.md) v2 | Symmetry fixes a subspace gradient descent keeps | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). Symmetries of the data confine population gradient descent to the weights those symmetries fix; for their task class and idealized architecture this is a subspace whose coordinates are interpretable head actions. It does not say the subspace is attractive (the paper proves only invariance), and it does not cover minibatch noise beyond expectation, learnable value maps (a sketch in the paper), or adaptive optimizers, which keep it only when the basis is coordinate-aligned. | Active |
| [THEORY-1052](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1052.md) | Rate tipping is failed time-scale separation | Ashwin, Wieczorek, Vitolo and Cox (2012), [LIT-1654](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1654.md), read in [NOTE-1215](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1215.md). Shown for the linear tipping-radius model, where the sufficient condition for tracking is a rate comparison, and stated for a fast-slow example ("rate dependent tipping occurs when the slow and very slow timescales are no longer separable"). Proposed because for nonlinear systems the paper says "no exact analogy possible" and gives no general condition. It bears on [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md), whose constraints hold over a window between time scales. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1054](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1054.md) v2 | Integrator, not coupling, picks wave vs heat | Spivak (2026), [LIT-1649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1649.md), read in [NOTE-1225](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1225.md) from arXiv v2. In the operad ArrSm, harmonic particles wired along a finite directed graph form one closed arrangement with potential Σ(κ_e/2)(q_tgt − q_src)². The phase semantics gives m_v q̈_v = −(L_G q)_v (Proposition 7.4.1) and a symplectic step; the configuration semantics gives m_v(q_v(t+1) − q_v(t)) = −(L_G q(t))_v (Remark 7.4.2). Active: both are short exact computations. It says nothing about time scales, and what differs between the two is a modelling choice, not the coupling. | Active |
| [THEORY-1056](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1056.md) | Spectral synchronization is near-optimal | Singer (2011), [LIT-1655](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1655.md), §§2, 4 and 5, read in [NOTE-1224](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1224.md) from arXiv v2. The threshold p > 1/√n comes from a cited rank-one deformation theorem adopted to a non-Gaussian mixture and a heuristic comparison with random correlation, confirmed by simulation at n = 100 and 400; the near-optimality ratio compares it with an information bound for a different success criterion. Proposed for both steps. It does not say that recovery is cheap on every graph, under every noise model, or for fine angular resolution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1057.md) | Backprop is functoriality of lens semantics | Spivak (2026), [LIT-1649](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1649.md), read in [NOTE-1225](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1225.md) from arXiv v2. Lens internalization (Corollary 3.3.4) and an integrator give operad functors ArrSm → PC (Theorem 4.3.6, Corollary 6.4.1). Under the configuration integrator the state update is q ↦ q − ♯_q(ξ_Q), with ξ_Q the Q*-component of the sum in (58); a parameterized map wired to a loss gives gradient descent (76), a weight-only potential gives weight decay (Proposition 7.2.3), and an inverse-Hessian response gives Newton's method (67). Active as mathematics. Per datum, deterministic, explicit-Euler; Adam and momentum are conjectures. | Active |
| [THEORY-1059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1059.md) v2 | Synchrony restricts to quotient network dynamics | Stewart, Golubitsky and Pivato (2003), [LIT-1674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1674.md), read in [NOTE-1217](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1217.md): the quotient construction (§7), Theorems 8.3, 8.4 and 9.2 with proofs, the counterexample of Remark 7.5 and Example 7.1. Active as mathematics. The quotient describes the dynamics on the invariant subspace exactly, but only a subclass of the quotient's own admissible dynamics arises that way, and nothing is said about stability transverse to the subspace. | Active |
| [THEORY-1060](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1060.md) v2 | Sheaf canonicity is axiomatic, not a theorem | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md) from arXiv v3. A textual finding about the paper, Active as such. The word "canonical" is never defined for sheaves as a sensor model; its technical uses are the standard ones for cohomology. It does not say that sheaves are a poor model, or that no theorem of this kind could be proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-1062](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1062.md) v2 | Sheaf diffusion permits stable polarization | Hansen and Ghrist (2020; SIAM J. Appl. Math. 2021), [LIT-1646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1646.md), §§2–4, read in [NOTE-1222](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1222.md) from the arXiv preprint. Active as mathematics: the convergence is a theorem about a linear heat equation, and the gap between expressed and held opinion is in the definitions and is worked in an example. It does not say that people reach agreement this way, or that an agreement in expression shows anything about what is held. | Active |
| [THEORY-1063](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1063.md) v2 | Circuit black-boxing is a functor | Baez and Fong (arXiv 2015, TAC 2018), [LIT-1644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1644.md), read in [NOTE-1223](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1223.md): Thm 1.1, proved as Thm 7.7, for circuits of passive, linear, two-terminal components over a field with positive elements, inductors and capacitors entering through the Laplace transform with zero initial conditions. The functor is not faithful, which is the point: circuits with one behaviour are identified. It says nothing about nonlinear or active components, and nothing in time-domain terms. | Active |
| [THEORY-1064](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1064.md) v2 | Spurious counterexamples locate missing splits | Clarke, Grumberg, Jha, Lu and Veith (2000), [LIT-1652](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1652.md), read in [NOTE-1231](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1231.md) from the authors' manuscript of the CAV paper. Active: the test for spuriousness (Lemma 1), the three-way cut at the failing state and the termination argument are given in full. The NP-hardness of the coarsest split is stated with its proof omitted, and the loop case rests on a theorem proved elsewhere. It does not say that the split found is the smallest, or how many rounds are needed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1065.md) | Robust synchrony iff balanced partition | Stewart, Golubitsky and Pivato (2003), [LIT-1674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1674.md), read in [NOTE-1217](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1217.md) from the accepted version: Theorem 6.5 with proof, Lemma 6.3, worked examples without symmetry (Figures 3, 9, 15, 19). Active as mathematics. It generalizes [THEORY-276](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-276.md)'s orbit clusters. "Robust" means invariant for the whole admissible class, not stable, and not invariant for one model family; the paper studies "existence, not stability". | Active |
| [THEORY-1067](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1067.md) v2 | Below threshold no estimator recovers the angles | Singer (2011), [LIT-1655](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1655.md), §5, read in [NOTE-1224](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1224.md) from arXiv v2. Active as mathematics: Fano's inequality applied to an explicit entropy count, asymptotic in m, n → ∞, p → 0 with L fixed. The bound is loose (it ignores the dependencies among offsets) and covers exact recovery and per-angle recovery, not partial correlation, which the eigenvector method achieves below it. It says nothing of what a bounded algorithm can do above it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1070](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1070.md) v2 | Sheaf heat flow projects onto cohomology | Hansen and Ghrist (2019), [LIT-1659](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1659.md), read in [NOTE-1233](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1233.md) from arXiv v2: Theorem 3.1 (discrete Hodge theory), H^0 ≅ Γ (p. 7) and Proposition 8.1 (the flow), each with a proof; Fig. 3.1 for the Laplacian not determining the sheaf. Active as mathematics. The paper does not speak of relaxation rates or time-scale separation, does not say what produces the restriction maps, and treats only linear flows of a fixed Laplacian. | Active |
| [THEORY-1077](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1077.md) v2 | Consistency radius bounds distance to sections | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), Definition 20 and Propositions 21 and 23, read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md) from arXiv v3; both proofs checked. Active as mathematics. It does not say that the nearest global section is unique (the paper's Proposition 25 claims so for Banach sheaves and the proof does not reach it), that the radius locates a fault, or that a small radius means the data are right. | Active |
| [THEORY-1079](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1079.md) v2 | Fast drift tips a stable attractor | Ashwin, Wieczorek, Vitolo and Cox (2012), [LIT-1654](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1654.md), read in [NOTE-1215](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1215.md) from the corrected arXiv v5. Active as mathematics: shown in a linear model with a fixed stable matrix (so no bifurcation and no noise), in normal-form examples worked exactly, and in a fast-slow system whose equilibrium is unique and globally stable. It does not say that a system that tips is lost for good, that the threshold is a basin boundary, or that any real system has tipped this way. | Active |
| [THEORY-1082](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1082.md) | Zero cycle holonomy iff twisted zero mode | Torres-Hugas, Duch, Gómez and Arenas (2026), [LIT-1668](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1668.md), read in [NOTE-1218](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1218.md) from the arXiv preprint v2. The criterion is stated in the paper with an energy argument (pp. 2–3) and is the standard one for discrete magnetic and connection Laplacians, which it cites; the spanning-tree step the paper omits is written out below. The isolated-cycle spectrum is in closed form (eqs. 29–32). Both were checked numerically. Active: a theorem, with the qualification that it concerns the relaxed linear problem, not the phase dynamics. | Active |
| [THEORY-1088](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1088.md) v3 | Diffusing expressions reach consensus by lying | Hansen and Ghrist (2020; SIAM J. Appl. Math. 2021), [LIT-1646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1646.md), §§8–9, read in [NOTE-1222](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1222.md) from the arXiv preprint. Active as mathematics: Theorems 8.1, 9.3 and 9.4 and Lemma 9.1. Theorem 9.3's proof is right only for α = β as printed; with the α, β weights it holds generally, which was checked numerically in the reading. The degeneracy guards are internal to the loop: minimal change and a conserved quantity, not evidence from outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1089](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1089.md) | Node elimination keeps Dirichlet forms | Baez and Fong (arXiv 2015, TAC 2018), [LIT-1644](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1644.md), read in [NOTE-1223](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1223.md): Thm 3.3, Lemma 3.4, Example 2.9 and Sec. 3.3. The elimination is what is usually called Kron reduction, a name the paper does not use. Over ℝ(s), with inductors and capacitors, the "minimum" is a formal stationarity condition, Kirchhoff's current law at interior nodes. The absence of identities is computed for a one-element set and asserted as typical otherwise. | Active |
| [THEORY-1090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1090.md) v2 | Kron reduction fails for sheaves in general | Hansen and Ghrist (2019), [LIT-1659](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1659.md), §4.2 (pp. 18–21), read in [NOTE-1233](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1233.md): a worked three-leaf star with a two-dimensional centre, and a closure theorem for the scalar-stalk case. Active as mathematics; the argument was checked. It is about the space of sections, a static fact; it does not say how often the obstruction arises, what structure would express the reduced constraint, or anything about dynamics. | Active |
| [THEORY-1092](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1092.md) | Discrepancies can pinpoint a faulty sensor | Robinson (2017), [LIT-1658](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1658.md), Example 24, Case 2 (pp. 26–28 of arXiv v3), read in [NOTE-1221](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1221.md). One simulated case, one noise realization, read from a figure. Proposed until a stated procedure is tested over trials, including faults in the restriction maps, which enter the discrepancies in the same way as faults in the data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1094.md) v2 | CEGAR revises the model, never the property | Clarke, Grumberg, Jha, Lu and Veith (2000), [LIT-1652](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1652.md), read in [NOTE-1231](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1231.md). A textual fact about the algorithm as specified in §§3–4, and the exact form of the limit the exchange of 2026-10-27 (A16 §6) gave for CEGAR as the formal neighbour of inquiry as specification ([CLAIM-470](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-470.md)). It does not say that a property cannot be revised by anyone, only that no step of this procedure does it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1096](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1096.md) | Garbling never improves attainable risk | Split from [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md) by the status review of 2026-10-27 ([ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md)). [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md)'s equivalence needs a second proof of the general converse and stays Proposed. Ten of its twelve dependents used only its definitions (an experiment, a garbling, the informativeness order), or only the easy direction, that a garbling never helps a decision-maker free to choose any rule. The easy direction holds on any outcome spaces, and its proof is two lines, re-derived below under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2's ruling, which [ADR-057](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-057.md) keeps. It is Theorem 3 of Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), read in [NOTE-595](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-595.md), and Blackwell's 1951 result. The finite converse is [THEORY-717](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-717.md), Active. | Active |
| [THEORY-1121](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1121.md) | GW barycenters can shrink or lose input structure | Peyré, Cuturi and Solomon (2016), [LIT-1797](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1797.md), Propositions 3–5 and Remark 3, read in [NOTE-1343](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1343.md) from the PMLR PDF. The closed forms and the cone preservation are proved and the PSD case was checked; the lack of guarantees is the authors' own statement. Active as a statement of what is and is not guaranteed. It does not say a barycenter erases minority structure; a toy run showed seed-dependent redistribution, not erasure. | Active |
| [THEORY-1123](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1123.md) | COTA's causal term is constant on its feasible set | Felekis, Zennaro, Branchini and Damoulas (CLeaR 2024), [LIT-1806](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1806.md), eqs. (6), (9), (10), (12) and Appendices A–B, read in [NOTE-1342](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1342.md) from the arXiv preprint v1. A derivation from the paper's own equations, which state the term as a divergence between column (or row) sums of two plans; Theorem 1's proof writes it the same way. Active as mathematics about the problem as written. The released code, read but not run, builds a different problem for posets with several chains, in which the term acts on copies of plans that carry no marginal constraints. | Active |
| [THEORY-1128](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1128.md) | Log co-occurrence of walks recovers geodesics | Hashimoto, Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola (2016), [LIT-1801](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1801.md), Lemma 1 and Corollary 6, read in [NOTE-1329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1329.md). Proved from the convergence of graph random walks to a diffusion and Varadhan's small-time formula, with an open conjecture needed for directed graphs; checked numerically on an unweighted ε-ball walk. Active as a theorem about the toy model. The authors say the model is not a model of language, and nothing here shows real corpora satisfy it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1129](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1129.md) | Fused GW anchors break ties only if they move | Derived from Vayer et al. (2019), [LIT-1813](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1813.md), Theorem 3.2's zero case, read in [NOTE-1328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1328.md); the paper does not state it. Checked by enumerating all 720 matchings of a 6-cycle with four anchor patterns. Active: an elementary consequence of a proved theorem, checked. It is about exact ties; with noisy data, symmetries become near-ties, and the theorem says nothing about how near. | Active |
| [THEORY-1130](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1130.md) v2 | GW distance is zero only for weak isomorphs | Chowdhury and Mémoli (2019), [LIT-1822](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1822.md), read in [NOTE-1330](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1330.md) from arXiv 1808.04337v2. Theorems 16 and 18, with full proofs in the main text (pp. 8–9). Active: proved. The sharp edge is the zero set. A distance of zero says the recorded weights and measures agree up to merging and splitting nodes with identical profiles; it says nothing about relations the record leaves out, and the measure is chosen by the user. | Active |
| [THEORY-1132](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1132.md) | Multi-marginal FGW is sum of pairwise objectives | Zeng et al. (2024), [LIT-1814](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1814.md), Theorem 1 and its proof (pp. 5, 12), read in [NOTE-1334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1334.md). The identity was checked numerically; the equality condition and the remark on composition are the record's, short consequences of it. Active. The edge: "consistent by construction" means jointly realizable, not composable, once couplings are soft; and the paper never reports the gap that measures how far independent pairwise optima are from joint realizability. | Active |
| [THEORY-1133](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1133.md) | GW identifies matches only up to automorphisms | Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola (2018), [LIT-1818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1818.md), use the GW objective (their eq. 8) for word translation and do not state its ambiguity; read in [NOTE-1336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1336.md). The invariance follows in two lines from the objective's form and was checked numerically, including a symmetric tree on which a branch-swapping coupling costs exactly what the true one does. Active: elementary and checked. It does not say how large the symmetry group of real embedding spaces is, and exact symmetries are rare in noisy data; near-symmetries give near-ties instead. | Active |
| [THEORY-1135](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1135.md) | OT under a global linear map is a GW problem | Alvarez-Melis, Jegelka and Jaakkola (2019), [LIT-1805](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1805.md), Lemmas 4.1–4.3 with proofs in Appendix D; read in [NOTE-1333](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1333.md). Each step was checked numerically. Active: proved, and checked. The conditions matter. The p = 2 link to GW holds for the original transport problem only when the target is whitened and all vectors have equal norm, which the paper states in two separate places. Nothing here makes the chosen class the right one for given data, and nothing in it is local. | Active |
| [THEORY-1136](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1136.md) | Poincaré embeddings differ by more than isometry | Alvarez-Melis, Mroueh and Jaakkola (2020), [LIT-1808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1808.md), §§5–7, Figs. 1–2, Tables 1–2; read in [NOTE-1323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1323.md). Proposed: single runs, one embedding method for the matching experiments, and GW, the obvious isometry-free baseline, is not run. It does not say why seeds disagree (the paper conjectures negative sampling), nor that the matching preserves the hierarchy's direction, which it does not enforce. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1138](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1138.md) | Lovász-cost OT stays convex if submodular | Alvarez-Melis, Jaakkola and Jegelka (2018), [LIT-1815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1815.md), §3, read in [NOTE-1324](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1324.md) from arXiv v1. The convexity and game form are standard submodular analysis; the failure of eq. (12) and the asymmetry were checked numerically. Active. It does not say structured couplings predict better; the experiments are single runs on 100 samples. | Active |
| [THEORY-1140](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1140.md) v2 | Frame symmetry leaves only holonomy invariants | Sarkar, Mukherjee and Sato (2026), [LIT-1820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1820.md), §2 and App. B, read in [NOTE-1331](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1331.md). The gauge-fixing argument is standard in lattice gauge theory and group synchronization, as the paper says, and its covariance was checked numerically here. Active: a conditional theorem. What it does not support is the paper's framing: "unique" holds for a family, and the antecedent is an inductive bias by the companion paper's own statement ([LIT-1803](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1803.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1141.md) v2 | Sheaf class sets which labellings diffusion splits | Bodnar, Di Giovanni, Chamberlain, Liò and Bronstein (NeurIPS 2022), [LIT-1811](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1811.md), §3.2 and Appendix B, read in [NOTE-1332](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1332.md) from the arXiv preprint v4. Active as mathematics: each separation result has a proof, and Propositions 9, 10 and 13 were checked numerically. The paper says the orthogonal construction exists only at d = 2 and 4; it exists at d = 8 as well, by the Hurwitz–Radon theorem, and was built. The results are existential: the separating sheaf is defined from the class labels, so they say what a sheaf can do, not that one can be found without the labels. | Active |
| [THEORY-1142](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1142.md) v2 | Satisfaction Condition lets provers be reused | Goguen and Burstall (1992), [LIT-1661](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1661.md), read in [NOTE-1348](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1348.md) from the published JACM article: Definition 32 (p. 125), Proposition 33 and Proposition 35 (p. 126), Theorem 39 (pp. 127–129). Active: proved, and checked on toy morphisms between propositional institutions. The collapsing morphism and the atom-negating morphism are my constructions, not the paper's. It is a criterion relative to a chosen model translation, and says nothing about translation beyond truth conditions. | Active |
| [THEORY-1147](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1147.md) | Entropic OT gradients come from one linear system | Yu et al. (2026), [LIT-1807](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1807.md), Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3 with Appendix A (pp. 4–5, 14–17), read in [NOTE-1327](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1327.md). Proved by implicit differentiation of the optimality conditions; checked by finite differences. Active. It is a derivative: a local, first-order estimate of a finite change, exact only for plain entropic OT whose cost does not depend on the plan. | Active |
| [THEORY-1149](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1149.md) | Co-OT bounds GW, equal for squared distances | Redko, Vayer, Flamary and Courty (2020), [LIT-1804](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1804.md), Propositions 2–3, read in [NOTE-1335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1335.md) from arXiv v3. Proved via Konno's theorem on concave quadratic programs and checked numerically, including strict inequality for non-Euclidean symmetric matrices. Active. It does not say COOT's two couplings coincide at every optimum, nor that either is unique. | Active |
| [THEORY-1150](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1150.md) | Institution theories glue wherever signatures do | Goguen and Burstall (1992), [LIT-1661](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1661.md), read in [NOTE-1348](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1348.md) from the published JACM article. Theorem 11 (p. 108) proves that the forgetful functor from theories to signatures reflects colimits, using only the Satisfaction Condition and the Closure Lemma; Proposition 23 and Theorem 24 (p. 119) extend it to theories with data constraints. Active: proved, and checked on a toy propositional institution. It does not say that signatures have colimits in a given logic, that the glued theory is consistent, or anything about proofs: closure is semantic. | Active |
| [THEORY-1152](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1152.md) | Strongest GW lower bound has a closed form | Chowdhury and Mémoli (2019), [LIT-1822](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1822.md), Theorem 24 and Lemma 28 (pp. 11–13), read in [NOTE-1330](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1330.md). Proved; the equalities were already known for discrete spaces from Schmitzer and Schnörr 2013, as the paper says. TLB = R-TLB and the order of the bounds were checked numerically on 25 random asymmetric pairs. Active. The edge the paper leaves implicit: a zero lower bound is no evidence of sameness. A 3-node pair with every bound zero is at dN,2 ≥ 0.215 (the record's construction). | Active |
| [THEORY-1155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1155.md) | COOT plans fixed only up to joint symmetries | Redko, Vayer, Flamary and Courty (2020), [LIT-1804](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1804.md), Proposition 1, read in [NOTE-1335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1335.md); the composition step is elementary and was checked by enumeration on small matrices, including a two-community block matrix with 32 tied optimal plan pairs. Active. It does not say real response matrices have exact symmetries; noisy ones give near-ties, which is the practical form of the threat. | Active |
| [THEORY-1156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1156.md) v2 | Fused GW interpolates Wasserstein and GW | Vayer, Chapel, Flamary, Tavenard and Courty (2019), [LIT-1813](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1813.md), Theorems 3.1–3.2 with the supplement's proofs, read in [NOTE-1328](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1328.md) from arXiv v3. Proved; the lower bound and the concavity in α of the exact value were checked on enumerated permutations. Active. It says nothing about the uniqueness of the optimal coupling or about the solver, which reaches only stationary points. | Active |
| [THEORY-1159](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1159.md) v2 | Joint three-network FGW alignment beats pairwise | Zeng et al. (2024), [LIT-1814](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1814.md), §5 and Appendix C, read in [NOTE-1334](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1334.md). Reported as plots against 13 baselines on ER, Douban, DBLP and ACM triples, with 10% anchors and 90% held out. Active as a report (ADR-065). Its ground truth is a consistent set of node triples, and no ablation holds the cost and the clustering fixed while changing joint for pairwise fitting, so the paper's attribution of the gain to joint fitting is THEORY-1210, Proposed. | Active |

The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2005](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2005.md) | Graph fibrations induce maps of network dynamics | From the reading of [LIT-2792](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2792.md) in [NOTE-2130](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2130.md). DeVille and Lerman (2013), arXiv 1303.3907. In a coordinate-free framework of networks of control systems on manifolds, they prove that a graph fibration (Boldi and Vigna's unique lifting of incoming edges, equivalently input-tree isomorphism) induces a map of dynamical systems in the opposite direction for every modular vector field. Surjective fibrations, which include quotients by balanced relations, embed the quotient's dynamics as an invariant synchrony polydiagonal. Injective fibrations project a network onto the subsystem that drives it, which they call an abstraction. Only this direction is proved, and stability is not treated. Here because it is the fibration form of the balanced-partition result held as [THEORY-1065](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1065.md) and [THEORY-1059](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1059.md), which it generalizes in one direction. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2022](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2022.md) | Defects classified by symmetry class and d − D | From the reading of [LIT-2797](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2797.md) in [NOTE-2124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2124.md). Teo and Kane (2010), arXiv 1006.0690 (Phys. Rev. B 82, 115120). A unified classification of defects in non-interacting insulators and superconductors. It uses the homotopy class of the Bloch or Bogoliubov–de Gennes Hamiltonian H(k, r) on a surface around the defect, which depends only on the symmetry class and δ = d − D, together with a generalized bulk-boundary correspondence, observed in examples rather than proved, that pairs a nontrivial class with protected gapless modes bound to the defect. In the Jackiw–Rebbi kink, the Jackiw–Rossi vortex and the dislocation, the defect's structural charge fixes the mode invariant. In a disordered weak topological insulator the protected modes outlive the structure that produced them. It is here for the relation between defect topology and bound modes ([CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md), [CLAIM-694](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-694.md)). It shows these are two topologies of different objects. What is protected is the hosted modes, not the defect's persistence. Skimmed in its NOTE. | Proposed |

Rudner, Lindner, Berg and Levin (2012; v2 2013), arXiv 1212.3324, published in Physical Review X 3, 031005 (2013). In periodically driven, non-interacting 2D lattices, chiral edge modes can exist when every Floquet band has Chern number zero. The bulk invariant that counts them is a winding number of the evolution operator over the whole driving period, not any property of the one-period Floquet operator. Two drives with the same stroboscopic bulk can have opposite edge chirality. It is here for interfaces between dynamically distinguished phases ([QUESTION-378](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-378.md), [QUESTION-490](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-490.md)). The paper establishes that phases can be told apart only by their intra- cycle dynamics, but it treats edges against vacuum, not interfaces between two driven regions. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |

Lohmiller, Slotine (1998), Automatica 34(6), DOI 10.1016/S0005-1098(98)00019-3, read from the authors' final manuscript (NSL-961001, December 1997) on the MIT Nonlinear Systems Laboratory site. It founds contraction analysis. If the generalized Jacobian F = (Θ̇ + Θ ∂f/∂x)Θ⁻¹ is uniformly negative definite in a metric M = ΘᵀΘ, all trajectories in a ball inside the region converge exponentially to one another, so initial conditions are forgotten. Conversely, every exponentially convergent system is contracting in some metric, and contraction survives parallel, skew- symmetric feedback and hierarchical combination, the last offered as a common frame for singular perturbations. Here because A29 grounded selective contraction in it; it is not the source of partial contraction toward invariant manifolds (that is Wang and Slotine 2005, not held), only of two remarks on convergence on a subspace. [THEORY-773](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md)'s disturbance lemma rests on its eq. (15). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2047](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2047.md) | Laplacian eigenmaps minimize Dirichlet energy | From the reading of [LIT-2794](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2794.md) in [NOTE-2120](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2120.md). Belkin, Niyogi (2001), Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 14 (NIPS 2001), read from the proceedings PDF on papers.nips.cc. Laplacian eigenmaps embed the vertices of a heat-kernel-weighted neighbourhood graph by minimizing the Dirichlet energy Σ(y_i − y_j)²W_ij under yᵀDy = I and yᵀD1 = 0, which gives the eigenvectors of Ly = λDy with the smallest non-zero eigenvalues. The constraints are there because the energy alone collapses every vertex onto a constant, and each connected component is treated separately. The graph Laplacian is argued, heuristically, to approximate the Laplace-Beltrami operator. The authors speculate that the natural clusters it brings out might ground perceptual categories. Here because A27 grounded the owner's U12 connection, dissipation of differences as self-supervised learning, in it ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19; [LIT-228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-228.md) holds the SSL equivalence). It has the energy and the collapse but no flow. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2287.md) v2 | Coexistence needs fitness ratio within overlap | Chesson (2011), restating his 1990 reworking of MacArthur. Then κ_j ρ / κ_i = α_ij/α_jj, and two species coexist when ρ < κ₁/κ₂ < 1/ρ. The overlap is unaffected by the heights of the consumption curves, which go into κ.
